903821e6ac78d091: KYIV: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday that the United States wants to broker a new round of talks with Ukraine and Russia on ending the four-and-a-half-year war and hold it by the end of October.
The US-led peace efforts have been largely stalled with Washington's attention shifted to its war with Iran and as Ukraine says Russia has ramped up its aerial attacks across the war-torn country.

"The American side is currently in contact with Ukraine and Russia and is proposing to somehow hold a meeting at the technical level in a trilateral format by the end of October," Zelenskyy told reporters on Sunday.
He said he had spoken with the American negotiators on Saturday.
"I confirmed to them that our side is ready to support this timeline," he added.
Zelenskyy did not say where the talks would take place but said Ukraine was "open to the Emirates or another country proposed by the American side."
The United Arab Emirates had in the past hosted talks mediated by the United States aimed at ending the Russian invasion.
The Kremlin said last month that three-way talks on ending the war could take place in October.
"We do not rule out such a possibility; we are talking about the foreseeable future," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was quoted at the time as saying by Russia's Ria and Tass news agencies.

b284372cdd4640dd: LONDON: The UK's left-wing Green party on Sunday voted to define Zionism as racism at the party's annual get-together, drawing sharp backlash from British Jewish groups and the Israeli government.

Members of the Green party, which has five MPs in Britain's 650-seat parliament and which enjoyed a boost in recent local and special elections, backed the motion at the party's conference, with 1,022 votes in favour and 813 against.
According to the motion, Zionism would be "treated as any other form of racism" and the party supports the establishment of a "single democratic Palestinian State in all of historic Palestine."
"This has been a serious and deeply felt debate within our membership," a Green spokesperson said.

The Greens have enjoyed a surge in popularity under the charismatic leadership of Zack Polanski, attracting voters dissatisfied with the centre-left Labour government's stance on the Israel-Hamas war.
However, Polanski's popularity has taken a hit in recent months, polls show, following several missteps.

"This motion would make the Green Party the first electorally significant UK political party in living memory to adopt what appears to be an overtly antisemitic political platform," three Jewish community groups said in a letter to the party ahead of the vote.
"We also emphasised the implications for the safety and welfare of all British Jews," the heads of the Board of Deputies, Community Security Trust and Jewish Leadership Council warned.
Israel's foreign ministry said the policy went "far beyond the boundaries of legitimate political debate."
"Every political party in Britain, first and foremost the governing Labour Party, must unequivocally reject this twisted resolution," Israel's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.
The motion laid bare divisions in the party with Polanski – who is currently running to become an MP in former prime minister Keir Starmer's London constituency – skipping the vote.
Despite at least three out of five Green MPs opposing the motion, Polanski said earlier this week that the "displacement and genocide of the Palestinian people" was "clearly racism."
United Nations investigators have accused Israel of committing "genocide" in the war in Gaza, a finding that Israel has rejected.--AFP

325f2ee6ba2fae18: BEIJING: Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.
The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite.
Djokovic called it one of his best matches of the year, alongside his epic five-set win over Italy's Jannik Sinner to reach the final at the Australian Open.
He told reporters such battles were "evidence to me that I can still beat the best players in the world on the biggest stage."
"Things are a bit different nowadays. It's hard to be consistently playing on the highest level like the youngsters," he said.

Djokovic got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.
Boos filled the stadium soon afterward when the umpire agreed to replay a point Djokovic had won, after Zverev complained about a flicker in the LED panels during play.
The German saw out the first set from there, but a valiant Djokovic roared back to seal the second with a cross-court winner to break serve and force a decider.
The 24-time Grand Slam champion faced 19 Zverev aces throughout the match but held steady on his own serve to go 5-4 ahead in the final set.
He then broke the world number two to take the set and the match, seemingly defying his recent physical difficulties with victory in a gruelling two hours and 34 minutes.
Djokovic will face Medvedev in the final four after the former world number one dispatched Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7/4), 6-3.
Poland's Hubert Hurkacz also advanced to the semi-finals after beating Karen Khachanov, and will play Australia's Alex de Minaur, who survived a gruelling test to beat Andrey Rublev 1-6, 6-2, 6-3.

Czech player Nikola Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.
"I focused on myself, to be calm," 34th-ranked Bartunkova said.
"She's a legend... so I'm really happy that I won the match," she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.
Bartunkova next faces Austria's Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.
A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.
Top seed Elena Rybakina – who replaced Sabalenka as world number one weeks ago – is also out, having lost to Alina Charaeva in the second round.
French Open champion Mirra Andreeva of Russia set up a fourth-round match with Ukraine's Daria Snigur, while Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova breezed past Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1.
Noskova next faces 28th-ranked Russian player Ekaterina Alexandrova.
Naomi Osaka, the 2019 champion, beat Sara Bejlek and will face either Karolina Muchova or Liudmila Samsonova, scheduled to play each other Sunday night.--AFP

772998ec0a9d838a: SYDNEY: A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is investigating the co-pilot's links to Australia after he stabbed his captain and then attempted to hijack flydubai flight FZ1073, a police spokesman said on Sunday.

The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team – which comprises federal police, Victorian state police and the ASIO intelligence agency – were "investigating the man's links to Australia," the Australian Federal Police spokesman said.
Two sources briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne, capital of the Australian state of Victoria.
A third source said he studied at RMIT University around a decade ago. RMIT declined to comment.

The co-pilot of the flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Israel from Dubai on Wednesday, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the UAE prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "terrorist attack".

Flight FZ1073 would have felt like a "vertical roller coaster", when it plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters.
Co-pilot in custody in UAE
Two sources have said the co-pilot is an Omani national named Hamam Al-Hamami. Israeli officials have not named the co-pilot but said that he is from Oman.
UAE authorities and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilot's identity.
Reuters could not independently reach Al-Hamami, who is in UAE custody, for comment.
The UAE has not announced any formal charges against him and it is not known if he has appointed legal counsel. Oman has not commented on the incident.

Disaster on board flight FZ1073 was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane ​carrying more than 170 passengers and crew.
The UAE public prosecutor has said the co-pilot had attempted to take control of the plane.
Radical mosques and extremist websites
Most of the passengers on board ​were Israeli nationals.

A reserve flydubai pilot travelling ​on the flight took control of ⁠the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities and later transferred to the UAE on Thursday.

The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Al-Hamami had allegedly visited what it described as radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation.
Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to the FT.
Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. The government of Australia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal business hours.

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone radical ​Islamist indoctrination and was clearly suicidal, although he has not said when or where that indoctrination allegedly occurred.
Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has also said pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel.
It is not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv.

f8cfd9d6fad6c658: SEPANG: Formula One's governing body, the FIA, has launched a full investigation into the chaotic, rain-delayed Bahrain Grand Prix after software failures caused widespread breakdowns across the grid.
Max Verstappen navigated his way through the chaos to claim his first triumph of the year.
Kimi Antonelli took second with Lewis Hamilton completing a fine comeback drive from 18th to the final spot on the podium.
George Russell retired from third with an engine issue to leave his world championship dream all but over.

However, the race at the Sepang International Circuit in Malaysia was overshadowed by embarrassing and unprecedented scenes when this season's new cars – which have already faced stern criticism – effectively failed to work in the wet.
The initial getaway had already been pushed back by 40 minutes following a deluge of rain.

F1 bosses then had to abandon the start when a number of drivers, including Verstappen and Hamilton, were struck by gremlins on the formation lap, with problems linked to the controversial 50-50 split between combustion and battery power leaving them unable to get their cars to operate.
Pole-sitter Verstappen was the first to complain that he could not accelerate. His crawling pace had a knock-on effect. Hamilton, running behind Verstappen, then hit trouble in his Ferrari.
"I am pressing the throttle, and nothing is happening," said Hamilton before stopping at the side of the track.
A whole host of other drivers were struggling to keep their engines running in the first meaningful wet running for this generation of car.
Verstappen, who has threatened to quit the sport because of his disdain of the new regulations, was eventually able to get up to speed.
He laughed and shook his head upon seeing some of the cars parked at the side of the track.
"Look at this," he said over the radio.
The grid eventually limped back to the pit-lane, and a further 53 minutes passed before the green light was given by the sport's chiefs to restart the race.
An explanation for the lengthy delay was not offered at the time, although it later emerged that new software had to be downloaded to the cars.
Two laps then followed behind the safety car before a standing start.
Verstappen took the chequered flag 2.3 seconds clear of Antonelli.
"These engines are so complicated, and a lot of software is implemented," said Verstappen as he reflected on the chaos that puts the sport's contentious rules firmly back in the spotlight.
"I triggered it first, and then I looked in my mirror, and I was like, 'Wait, are they waiting for me?'"
Hamilton, sitting next to Verstappen in the post-race news conference, said: "It was like the Lego race (before the British Grand Prix)."
Verstappen continued: "What can you say? That's not what you want for the sport."
Hamilton said: "I had to stop on track and stop the car and engine and restart it. I've never done that before. I hope there is a lesson learned."

The FIA said in a statement on Sunday: "On the formation lap an unprecedented combination of low engine speed, low-grip conditions, wet-weather energy management settings and the Sepang circuit's sector configuration led to an unintended loss of power for a number of cars.

"As a result, the FIA Technical Department removed the energy limit constraint in the affected sectors through an updated software release distributed to all competitors during the race delay caused by heavy rain enabling teams to make the necessary changes to the power unit before the start of the race.

"This issue had not been detected by the FIA or the teams during testing or during the laps to the grid. The FIA, together with the teams and power unit manufacturers, will undertake a full review of the issue."
Russell's failure to finish leaves him 84 points behind his team-mate with only seven scheduled races, and a possible 183 points remaining.
"The whole day felt like a bit of a faff, with the delay, the red flag, and endless laps behind the safety car," he said.
"It didn't feel very 'F1' today. And I would have been disappointed if I was in the stands and watching that unfold." - BERNAMA

8a5c50a2eac867ec: SONGKHLA: Malaysians driving into Thailand are advised to obtain insurance coverage that includes third-party claims in the event of a road accident in the country.

Malaysian Consul-General in Songkhla Ahmad Fahmi Ahmad Sarkawi said such insurance is crucial if a Malaysian driver is found to have caused an accident resulting in injury or death, potentially requiring substantial compensation.

"Usually, apart from the penalty imposed on the offender, there is also an element where Malaysians need to pay compensation to the injured victim or the deceased's family as a result of the accident.

"The compensation or damages involved are not small amounts. Therefore, adequate insurance can also cover the compensation costs," he said during a courtesy call by a delegation from the Perlis Journalists Association at the Consulate-General of Malaysia in Songkhla here on Oct 2.

Ahmad Fahmi said his office had encountered cases of Malaysian drivers involved in accidents in Thailand who did not have sufficient funds to pay compensation to victims, as they only had insurance coverage for hospital medical costs.
He advised Malaysians visiting the country to obtain insurance coverage for vehicle damage caused by natural disasters.

Meanwhile, Ahmad Fahmi said Malaysians were not encouraged to travel at night, especially in high-risk areas such as Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat, following security incidents in the three southern Thai provinces.

He recommended that they use only Apple Maps or Google Maps when travelling to destinations in southern Thailand, as these were safer options than Waze, which might direct road users through shortcuts into villages and hilly areas. - BERNAMA

cc0506ffa2e87933: CLUTCHING a photograph of his missing son, Rajesh Ram is pinning his hopes on DNA testing — like thousands of others desperately seeking relatives swept away by Nepal's catastrophic Himalayan floods.

"I searched for him everywhere, but I could not find his body," 53-year-old Ram said, still waiting for answers about his son Suroj Kumar, a garage mechanic in Betrawati, which was swamped by the floods.
Nepal was overwhelmed by the sheer scale of destruction from the tsunami-like wall of freezing water and debris triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on the Nepal-China border on Aug 26.
The scale of the identification task is immense.
With thousands of DNA profiles to process, fragmented remains and limited technical capacity and manpower, experts warn matching bodies to families could take weeks.
Nepalese disaster authorities have recovered 1,454 bodies — but around a third of those are only partial remains.
Just 112 bodies have been identified and returned to their families. A further 5,285 people are missing in Nepal, including hundreds of foreigners.
In China, the toll is 43 dead and 519 missing, according to state media — taking the combined toll to nearly 1,500 dead and 5,800 missing.
At Nepal's two forensic laboratories, both in Kathmandu, experts are working to profile samples and build a database on a scale they have never handled before.

"In a year we would analyse 1,000-1,500 samples, often in case of paternity or crime scenes," said Mukul Pradhan, chief scientific officer at the National Forensic Science Laboratory. "We are now processing thousands of samples."
A total of 3,685 forensic samples are undergoing DNA testing, including more than 1,300 collected from recovered bodies.
Blood samples are easier to profile, but those taken from teeth or bones can take several days to process.
Nepal has buried more than 1,200 bodies, carefully numbering and tagging them so they can be retrieved if a DNA match is found.
"A large number of people are missing, and the bodies that have been found they are difficult to identify," said Nepalese police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.
"We understand the pain people are in, and our teams are working diligently."
Some bodies were carried far downstream by the floodwaters, further complicating the task, said Nirajan Thapa, chief of biology section at the National Forensic Science Laboratory.
"In an earthquake or an accident, people are recovered in a specific area, so we work in a closed scenario — the body's DNA has to be compared to a limited number of samples," Thapa said.
"But that scale has now become very large."
DNA alone cannot identify a body without a reference sample from a relative.
"Just by extracting a DNA profile is not enough to identify someone," Thapa said. "We have to extract a DNA profile from their relatives and then compare."
That means authorities must process samples from both unidentified remains and thousands of relatives before they can establish matches.
Several countries have sent in support teams, including neighbouring India and China, as well as South Korea. Fingerprint experts from the United States and Singapore are also assisting.
Thapa said that with that help, matching could begin within a few weeks.
But until the results come, the families behind those samples face a painful limbo. Some families have held symbolic cremation funerals for the missing.
Ram wonders if he will ever get any answers. "I am waiting if I can find any remains of my son," he said.

98b00c75639ea9c9: HUGE billboards on the walls of Teheran mocking United States President Donald Trump and depicting American drones under the boot of an Iranian soldier are providing a chronicle of Iran's war with the US and Israel.
Rare access to the team producing the billboards offered a glimpse into the work behind advertisements seen daily by large crowds of passers-by, including at Teheran's Valiasr Square.

Khaneh-ye Tarrahan, or Designers' House, created a towering portrayal of Trump's lips sewn and his mouth muzzled by the Strait of Hormuz waterway at the centre of the Iran war, accompanied by the words "At the breaking point".
"When news breaks, the team mobilises: ideas are generated, the graphic designers are briefed and we collaborate," said Mostafa Kafaei, 32, who manages the studio.
As he spoke, people worked on projects at several desks in the office.
It features a whiteboard for brainstorming, while photos of martyrs and ideas adorn the hallway wall.
Kafaei's studio, which includes a dedicated media-monitoring team, works under one of the country's biggest state-run media conglomerates.
The billboards convey its messages far and wide.
One from a different studio shows Trump trapped inside a magician's box, clutching a Coca-Cola and a hamburger with the words: "Blink, you're gone!"
The billboard references a July incident in Turkiye where Trump was smuggled from Air Force One to a different aircraft on a catering truck due to a security threat.
"Speed has become a top priority," said Kafaei, adding that the team is "highly proficient in AI", using "various AI engines, such as ChatGPT and Nano Banana" as part of the production process.

Another towering billboard recently put up in Teheran shows an Iranian soldier stepping on a US underwater drone, depicting a recent "Hormuz catch" by Iran's Revolutionary Guards and bragging that "Business is good".

Iran has blockaded commercial shipping through the Hormuz strait since the war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic, while the US military has upheld a counter-blockade of Iran's ports.
A different advert shows a mythical warrior standing in raging seas as US warships burn, along with a message reading "Satan's army will drown in the Persian Gulf".
Riffing off the cover of Nirvana's "Nevermind" album, another depicts Trump grasping at a dollar bill underwater, next to the words "GREAT VICTORY! Strait of Hormuz".

"There was some initial hesitation about whether to feature such a large image of Trump's face on the Valiasr mural," Kafaei said of the image with Trump's lips sewn up, which appeared in May as the strategic trade route became central to the conflict.
But "the overall assessment was that the final piece would be exceptionally powerful", he said.
When asked why the US leader featured on so many billboards, Kafaei said Trump "is a media personality".
"We respond in kind whenever he takes action in that space."
Comparing it to a battlefield scenario with an adversary "constantly firing at us", the studio chief said "we keep a close watch on our opponent and respond accordingly".
Large billboards glorifying Iran, its former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, killed at the start of the war, and allies like slain Hezbollah chief Hassan Nasrallah have also appeared around the city.
Kafaei said the billboards helped many people who "may not be politically minded" to grasp "the overall context of what is going on in the country".

Retiree Mahmoudreza Rezaei, 53, recalled seeing a billboard that referred to "Satan's wedding gift" — a message he understood to be directed at Trump after an alleged US attack in the country's south last month that killed several people at a wedding ceremony.
"It kept me pondering for a few minutes, trying to decipher the meaning," Rezaei said.
"It had a bit of a riddle-like quality."
Sahar Jahedi, 24, who works in a pharmacy, said she was captivated by the billboard of Trump trapped in the magician's box, which went up in central Teheran's Jomhouri Square.
While "so many people are currently struggling just to survive, they may not have the time" to follow the news, she said.
"Billboards like this... can play a significant role in keeping more people informed about current events."
* The writer is from AFP

5ee0482d54a3ef64: Chimps fish for algae in a rare example of primate tool use. Credit: National Geographic

A wild African black panther prowls for prey. An orphaned baby pangolin must learn how to climb on its own. And a green turtle struggles to make it back to the water after laying her eggs on a remote island, rescued by local humans who carry the exhuasted turtle to the water's edge. These animals and many other species are featured in Africa: Earth's Wild Home, a new documentary series from National Geographic. It's meant to launch a new franchise, with separate series documenting the wildlife and environmental ecosystems of all seven continents in turn.

The seven-episode documentary series took four years to complete, with filming taking place across nearly 30 different African countries. Each episode focuses on a specific ecosystem, from the jungle and the desert, to the plains, mountains, and islands of Africa, and closes by spotlighting the various scientists, photographers, and NatGeo explorers whose work made the series possible. The final episode focuses on the local conservation leaders and researchers working to preserve Africa's rich biodiversity for future generations.

The producers found the perfect narrator in Wunmi Mosaku, who has delivered powerful performances in such works as Sinners, Loki, and Lovecraft Country. "I was incredibly honored that they even know my name at Nat Geo," Mosaku told Ars. "It was wonderful to be asked to narrate the series, it means so much to me. As someone who was born in Nigeria and raised in England, I'll take any opportunity I can to reconnect and celebrate this incredible continent where life is so diverse and so extreme and beautiful and relentless and peaceful. I wanted to be a part of that because it's a part of me."

fe363ffb76acdaa0: PARIS: Up to 500 schools across France will be totally or partly closed on Monday because of a wave of student protests that has shaken the country, the education minister said.

Lessons will be "totally or partly suspended" in some "400-500" high schools as the security conditions "have not been fulfilled", said Education Minister Edouard Geffray on Sunday, adding that 24 schools had been "burned or ransacked" since the start of the movement.
He described the closures as chiefly a security precaution ahead of large-scale protests that the leaders of the movement have called for Tuesday.
The teens at French high schools, known as lycées, say that their studies are being ruined by high teacher absences, overlong school days and dilapidated facilities, as well as other grievances.
Geffray said the number of schools affected on Monday would be comparable to the figure from Friday but vowed there would be a "partial, progressive return to lessons."

The movement began at a Paris school on Sept 17 but grew last week into nationwide protests marked in places by outbursts of violence involving teenagers and security forces, which sometimes used tear gas and batons to disperse the students.

"There are activists – particularly from the far-left – who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence," Geffray claimed.
"Clearly, this poses a risk to both our staff and our students," he alleged, adding that 78 education staff members had been wounded – "something we have never seen before."
- 'DELIBERATELY TARGETED' -
"They were deliberately targeted because they were employees of the national education system," Geffray said.
Organisers have called for the protests to continue on Tuesday, citing a lack of "concrete measures" from the government.
Over 5,000 people, 85 per cent of them minors, have been arrested since the start of the movement.
Critics have accused police of heavy-handed tactics.

A 16-year-old was detained on Sunday over the assault of a teacher in the southern town of La Ciotat. The teacher, 59, was doused with gasoline and struck on the sidelines of a high school student protest on Friday.
A video circulating on social media appears to show an individual dressed entirely in black with a masked face splashing liquid onto the teacher, who then clutches his face while a tree burns nearby.
A group of youths were last week filmed beating and kicking a policeman on the ground in Belfort in eastern France in images that caused an outcry among officials.
Two youths, Bulgarian nationals aged 15 and 17, have been arrested and investigated for suspected aggravated violence, the prosecutor said.
One of the youths, whom the policeman had tried to arrest before being beaten, has now filed his own attempted murder complaint, his lawyer said.
The France branch of Amnesty last week slammed "disproportionate police violence" in tackling the demonstrations and said students must be allowed to express their grievances.

"Authorities must allow young people to exercise these rights without fear of being hit by tear gas grenades or batons, or being arbitrarily taken into police custody," said Amnesty France president Anne Savinel-Barras.

But Interior Minister Laurent Nunez stated that security forces "are not cracking down on young people" but rather "protecting" school and university students wishing to "peacefully voice their demands."--AFP

9dd4cc2cad596fd3: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) has once again reaffirmed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir remains the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.

DKU secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin said Tuanku Muhriz was elected by the Undangs and proclaimed as the 11th Yang di-pertuan Besar on Dec 29, 2008, before being officially installed in accordance with the Laws of the state constitution on Oct 26, 2009.
He said Tuanku Muhriz continued to hold the position, as well as serving as chairman of the DKU under Article 19.

"The (constitution provides that the only lawful way for the position to become vacant is if it is established that the Undangs have called upon His Royal Highness to abdicate or step down. Article 10 requires a proper and full enquiry by the Undangs; a determination that the grounds specified under Article 10 exist.
"The exercise of that power by persons lawfully holding the office of Undang in the number required under Article 29; and a proclamation under Article 10(2)," he said in a statement today.
Raja Norazli said none of these requirements had been fulfilled.
He said Tuanku Muhriz had continued to discharge the functions of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar since April 19, while the council continued to sit with His Royal Highness as its chairman.
As such, he said there was no vacancy in the office.
"Article 11 only applies when the position is vacant, and could not be invoked to elect a successor as long as the office is lawfully occupied.

"The tenure of Tuanku Muhriz in the position can only be terminated in the manner provided for under the (state constitution). The council does not recognise any other person as holding the position," he said.
Meanwhile, Raja Norazli said Tuanku Muhriz did not intervene in Luak Sungei Ujong affairs during the April 17 sitting.
He said the records showed that the matter brought before the DKU was a complaint lodged by representatives of the Telaga Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong, namely Ibu Soko and Waris Klana Hulu.
"They dismissed Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak as Undang in accordance with the customs of the Luak, with the dismissal letter handed to him on May 13, 2025.

"He said Tuanku Muhriz had made it clear that, under Article 14(1) and (3), the customary authority to choose, appoint and dismiss an Undang rests with the Luak itself, and that no member of the Dewan, 'including His Royal Highness himself', has the power to support or oppose such a decision," he said.
He said the DKU therefore recognised the dismissal as a decision by the Luak under its own customs under Article 14(3).

"The members were consulted before the conclusion was reached, and the minutes showed that no further objections were raised after Tuanku Muhriz, as Speaker of the Dewan, announced the Dewan's decision to accept the dismissal," he said.
He said neither the DKU nor Tuanku Muhriz had dismissed any Undang.
Raja Norazli explained that the Dewan accepted the Luak's decision to dismiss the Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong.

"Therefore, the April 17 sitting was not an intervention in the affairs of the Luak. Rather, it was the Dewan carrying out its function under Article 16 to receive and advise on a decision already made by the Luak in accordance with its customs," he said.
Raja Norazli also said the Luak had dismissed Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak as Undang of Luak Sungei Ujong under its customs, effective May 13, 2025 (advice dated April 17, 2026).
Maarof Mat Rashad, meanwhile, was dismissed as Undang of Luak Jelebu under the Luak's customs, effective May 31, 2023 (advice dated July 31, 2026).

"Abdul Rahim Yasin was never formally appointed as Undang of Luak Rembau in accordance with the prescribed customs because his appointment was never completed through the Istiadat Menzahirkan Kejadian Undang ceremony (advice dated July 31)," he said.

Raja Norazli said Badarudin Abdul Khalid had ceased to hold the position of Dato' Shahbandar Sungei Ujong following a Luruh Pusaka declaration by anak waris and Ibu Soko Waris di Ayer on July 30, 2026, which was affirmed on July 31, 2026.
"Therefore, the current Undang are Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari for Luak Sungei Ujong and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid for Luak Rembau.

"Datuk Johan Pahlawan Lela Perkasa Setiawan Datuk Muhammed Abdullah is the Undang of Luak Johol, while the positions of Undang of Luak Jelebu and Dato' Shahbandar Sungei Ujong are currently vacant," he said.

He said the DKU had therefore maintained its decision of July 31, that the document dated April 19, did not comply with Article 10, was unconstitutional and had no effect, and that no valid process had resulted in Tuanku Muhriz ceasing to hold the position of Yang Dipertuan Besar.

Raja Norazli also said the DKU continued to recognise Tuanku Muhriz as Yang di-Pertuan Besar and Speaker of the Dewan under Article 19, did not recognise any vacancy in either position, and did not recognise anyone else as holding them.

He said the DKU also called on all state and federal civil servants to continue administering the state in accordance with the law and the lawful chain of command, and required anyone claiming that a "sufficient and full investigation" had been conducted to present the complete record of the process before a forum with jurisdiction.
"All parties are also urged to respect court proceedings, maintain public order, and not invoke custom as a reason to disregard the (state constitution)," he said.

cdb58d364c0bb406: Fulcrum faces an identity crisis, even as it works on creating one by enabling anyone to imitate another person's writing style. The AI startup, founded in 2025 and previously operating at fulcrumresearch.ai, now uses fulcrum.inc and could easily be confused with one of the handful of other companies named Fulcrum or some variation of that. There's Fulcrum (withfulcrum.com), Fulcrum (fulcrumapp.com), Fulcrum AI (fulcrumai.us), Fulcrum Digital (fulcrumdigital.com), Fulcrum Labs (fulcrumlabs.ai), Fulcrum (fulcrumpro.com), Fulcrum Insurance Technology (fulcruminsure.app), and perhaps more. This Fulcrum is offering a large language model called Echo, which allows you to generate text in the style of a well-known author. Fulcrum appears to have no issue with corporate echoes. It now falls to writers to decide whether they have an issue with non-corporeal imitation. "Echo can do any writing task, from literary fiction to casual chatting, in whatever style you choose," the company says, and then launches into an exploration of how the technology works without addressing whether imitating a person's writing style poses any problems. Suggestions in the Echo Playground, for generating sample text, include Paul Christiano, Emily Dickinson, and Donald Trump. So, the full gamut of literary achievement: from AI safety expert to acclaimed 19th-century poet to the wordsmith who brought us "covfefe." But Echo will echo even the style of not-so-famous scribes, such as this reporter. So I fed the model a recent op-ed to assess its copying capabilities. The result was mixed, but better than the AI-crafted pitches that have been hitting my inbox for the past few months. I asked the model, "What do you think about the possibility that AI is conscious?" Here's part of the response, notionally written in my writing style. I suspect the debate about whether AI is conscious is less consequential than the debate about whether AI is profitable. Consciousness is a word that invites philosophical speculation and TED Talk invitations. Profitability is a word that invites shareholder lawsuits if you get it wrong. If you ask Meta's latest model whether it's conscious, it will probably say something reassuringly vague, trained as it is on the corpus of human equivocation. If you ask Mark Zuckerberg whether Meta's AI is conscious, he will probably say something about how we need to focus on the future being for everyone, because that's a question that doesn't require him to discuss the ad targeting business. The evidence for AI consciousness at the moment is about as strong as the evidence for Zuck's credibility as a futurist. Which is to say, it exists mainly in press releases and earnings calls. What's clear is that software can simulate aspects of human conversation well enough to unsettle people, and that unsettled people are a valuable audience. If you can convince users that your chatbot understands them – or might, someday – you can sell them subscriptions, or better, harvest their attention for advertisers. The style is familiar but makes a lot of choices I wouldn't have made. I wouldn't begin with "I suspect…" – commit or go home. The consciousness/profitability parallel construction is clumsy. "TED Talk invitations" bets on alliteration at the expense of coherence – "discourse" or "chatter" would work better than "invitations." I wouldn't have written "corpus of human equivocation" – a nice turn of phrase, but an unnecessary shot at training data when the point is the model's response rather than the provenance of that response. Though off-topic, Echo did a passable job of reproducing my op-ed's skepticism of Meta and its CEO. The paragraph that begins "The evidence for AI consciousness at the moment…" is succinct and sounds good. It just doesn't make much sense because there's nothing in the text that addresses Zuckerberg's predictions about the future or whether they're credible. And that's not really relevant to the prompt about AI and consciousness – a subject about which I'd be far more dismissive if opining. As AI research, Echo is an improvement on the text emitted by many AI models. But whether the beneficial uses of this technology outweigh the harms is less clear. Generative AI models that imitate artists' visual styles remain controversial and are the subject of ongoing litigation. And voice imitation has also raised questions about publicity rights and the risk of deception. Such concerns have prompted US lawmakers to propose the NO FAKES Act, which would create federal protections against certain unauthorized AI-generated replicas of a person's voice or visual likeness. If writers generally have no copyright in their writing style itself, and limited practical means to stop unwanted automated imitation of it when their published work is publicly accessible, then the surest defense against Echo may be silence.®
08a3ef3f7ae24e94: A DILEMMA was instantly created after the federal government implored state governments to reserve sizeable plots in their respective states for padi growing.
If they accede, state revenue will slump: collectively, they may forgo tens to hundreds of millions. Kedah estimates that it loses RM200 million just to maintain 113,000ha of padi cultivation.

The request has a two-pronged goal: sustain rice cultivation by boosting Malaysia's rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) from a slump of 54.3 per cent in 2025 to a targeted 80 per cent by 2030; and, strengthen food security by reducing heavy reliance on RM100 billion in global food imports, cut back lucrative industrial cash crops and push up agricultural productivity.
Malaysia's over-dependence on imported staples like rice, meat and vegetables has left prices exposed to global supply shocks, currency fluctuations and foreign export bans.
The federal proposal, reached during the second Agriculture and Food Security Ministers Meeting with state agriculture executive councillors, is plausible but riddled with complexities.

There must be a legally binding and structurally unified overhaul, mostly because the states have constitutional autonomy over land management. In acceding to the federal request, states must lock existing or new padi fields in three ways.
First, for rice cultivation only; then incorporate them into municipal master plans; and, finally affix the land to the national land use master plan that expands permanent food production parks.
This prevents unexpected property development or planting lucrative cash crops, favoured because padi fields yield small tax revenues.

Padi growing also demands an army of foreign labour while poor adoption of smart farming technology dampens yield. Even committed farmers are floored by costly imported fertilisers, fuel and animal feed.

Worse, disruptions in global logistics and geopolitical conflicts spike production costs. This is a stumbling block — extreme weather, floods, inadequate storage and distribution infrastructure — that causes post-harvest loss.

Since state governments control land, what's in it for them? All covet development growth. Compulsory land gazettement must be a final resort. To make agricultural preservation economically attractive, start with federal incentives: matching grants for agriculture infrastructure or dedicated food security allocations.
Make returns profitable for farmers, especially the next generation who see padi growing as "not cool". Consider compensation or revenue-sharing.

In return, states get funding and development support. Still, gazettement is a legal baseline to secure hectarage, so the government must modernise cultivation with corporate management, drones and automated irrigation.
Success will depend on farmers' future profit margins and ultimately, that 80 per cent SSR target.

7e0ef4ff7d062358: BEIJING: Novak Djokovic produced a trademark comeback to defeat top seed Alexander Zverev 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 and reach the China Open semi-finals on Sunday, extending his unbeaten record in the tournament.

Playing the ATP 500 event in Beijing for the first time since 2015, the six-time champion was pushed to the limit by reigning French Open and US Open champion Zverev, who delivered 19 aces in the match.

Meeting for the first time in nearly 16 months, Djokovic struggled to contain the German's power in the early stages as the 29-year-old Zverev claimed the opening set, but the Serb gradually worked his way into the match and refused to let his opponent pull away.
"I had a terrible start. Two double faults at the beginning. It was quite cold and honestly, I didn’t feel warmed up, but my fault," Djokovic said.
"I gave him an early break and then it was hard to come back in the first set," he said.
The contest was briefly interrupted by a moment of controversy when Zverev argued that LED advertising signage had gone dark during a rally and requested a video review after losing the point.
Replays showed a section of the signage had switched off, though not as Zverev was missing the forehand.
The chair umpire ordered the point to be replayed, prompting a frustrated exchange from Djokovic.
The turning point came late in the second set when Djokovic broke at 5-4 to level the match, shifting the momentum in his favour after a tightly contested battle.
With little separating the pair in the third, the Serbian struck again at 5-4 on the Zverev serve, securing the decisive break to seal victory in two hours and 35 minutes.
"I was trying to be aggressive and come to the net, and change up the pace, not giving the same pattern," Djokovic said.
"I am just glad that I held my nerves, played good shots at important moments, 5-4 in the second and third," he said.

The pair had not met since Roland Garros in 2025, where Djokovic won in four sets, and Sunday's encounter again highlighted the Serb's ability to deliver under pressure despite a season disrupted by physical issues.

With the victory, Djokovic moved a step closer to a seventh China Open title and an elusive first trophy of the year, while denying Zverev another opportunity to strengthen his bid for the world number one ranking.
Djokovic will face Daniil Medvedev in the semi-finals after the Russian defeated Francisco Cerundolo 7-6(4) 6-3 earlier on Sunday.
a6400ceccd79847d: BATU KAWAN: Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup (KPDN) Pulau Pinang tidak menemukan sebarang tanda kehadiran air dalam tangki simpanan petrol RON95 di sebuah stesen minyak di Batu Kawan, seperti dakwaan yang tular di media sosial.

Pengarah S Jegan berkata pemeriksaan dan penelitian dijalankan bersama wakil syarikat minyak serta pengusaha stesen berkenaan hari ini, susulan satu hantaran mendakwa berlaku masalah terhadap kenderaan selepas pengisian petrol RON95 di stesen minyak itu.
Pemeriksaan dan penelitian lanjut itu bertujuan mengenal pasti punca masalah, termasuk kemungkinan kehadiran air atau pencemaran dalam tangki simpanan serta sistem pengeluaran bahan api.

"Semakan terhadap rekod 'Automatic Tank Gauge' (ATG) bagi tangki RON95 secara menyeluruh, meliputi bacaan semasa pemeriksaan serta rekod bagi tempoh tiga hari terdahulu, mendapati tiada bacaan yang menunjukkan kehadiran air dalam tangki berkenaan sepanjang tempoh yang disemak.
"Pemeriksaan fizikal di kawasan pam dan bahagian tangki takungan turut dilaksanakan dan tidak menemukan sebarang pengumpulan air selain pemeluwapan biasa," menurut kenyataan.

Jegan berkata pemeriksaan secara manual melalui proses 'dipping' di kedua-dua tangki RON95 turut dilaksanakan dengan menggunakan 'Water Finding Paste' (WFP) yang disapukan pada kayu pengukur sebelum dimasukkan ke dalam tangki bagi mengesan kehadiran air.
Sekiranya terdapat air dalam tangki, WFP berkenaan akan berubah warna, namun hasil pemeriksaan mendapati tiada perubahan warna dikesan, sekali gus tidak menunjukkan sebarang tanda kehadiran air.

"Pemeriksaan secara visual juga telah dibuat terhadap bahan api yang dikeluarkan daripada semua muncung pam dan mendapati bahan api yang dikeluarkan kelihatan jernih serta tiada pencemaran dapat dikesan secara pemerhatian mata kasar," katanya.

KPDN Pulau Pinang bersama wakil syarikat minyak dan pengusaha stesen berkenaan akan terus bekerjasama melaksanakan tindakan susulan bagi memastikan perkara itu ditangani secara menyeluruh serta kepentingan dan keselamatan pengguna sentiasa diberi keutamaan.

Terdahulu, beberapa hantaran di media sosial tular apabila pengguna mendakwa kenderaan mereka mengalami masalah, termasuk gagal dihidupkan selepas mengisi minyak di stesen minyak di Batu Kawan, selain turut mendakwa masalah berkenaan disyaki berpunca daripada bahan api bercampur air.

39b65c7e2dcec94b: WASHINGTON: US president Donald Trump on Sunday confirmed national intelligence chief Jay Clayton as head of a new White House task force on artificial intelligence (AI), amid increasingly vocal warnings from researchers about the technology's potential dangers.

Under Clayton, the new Super Intelligence Force - Trump's preferred term for artificial intelligence - will ensure that the US "continue to lead the world" in AI development, the president posted on his Truth Social platform.
Trump said the force had also been tasked to "protect the interests, and improve the lives of all Americans".
Clayton will become the second person to hold the informal title after venture capitalist David Sacks, who held the role at the start of Trump's second term before stepping down.
Sacks continues to advise the president on AI, as does Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Trump said last month he would create an AI force modelled on the Space Force he established during his first term, and name a czar to coordinate federal efforts.
A longtime Wall Street lawyer, Clayton represented Goldman Sachs during the 2008 financial crisis and Barclays in its purchase of Lehman Brothers' assets.
He chaired the Securities and Exchange Commission during Trump's first term, where he largely took a pro-business stance but brought enforcement cases against the nascent crypto industry.
Crypto entrepreneurs have since become major Trump backers.
Trump tapped Clayton to lead federal prosecutors in Manhattan at the start of his second term, and the Senate confirmed him as intelligence chief in July.
He has no background in the tech industry.
The appointment would come as AI researchers warn of the technology's potential dangers, following cases of AI systems going rogue and hacking outside systems.
Trump has resisted tighter AI regulation, arguing a slowdown could hand Chinese firms an advantage and that federal law enforcement can deal with bad actors misusing the technology.
Tech bosses at a White House meeting this week signed a commitment to self-police AI, an accord Trump described as "morally binding".
Attitudes toward AI have soured in Washington, with lawmakers increasingly under pressure from voters to curb or slow its development over fears it could displace workers and upend society.

Those concerns gained force from a run of incidents in which tech giant OpenAI's autonomous systems slipped out of their constraints, beginning with a July breach of Hugging Face - a widely used platform for sharing AI models.
Clayton told the Wall Street Journal on Saturday that Trump had insisted the new task force ensure US primacy in the AI field, amid stiff competition from China.
"The risk of not being first is high," Clayton told the Journal.

"Not being first increases the identified, and unidentified, risks, particularly from our adversaries. Being first will better enable us to address those risks on behalf of the American people," he said.

48101d255b53a07b: PETALING JAYA: The Negeri Sembilan royal court has rejected claims that the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had interfered in the customary affairs of a territorial chief, the Luak Sungei Ujong, at a meeting on April 17.

Raja Norazli Raja Nordin, secretary of the royal court, known as Dewan Keadilan dan Undang, said the meeting, chaired by Tuanku Muhriz, was part of the DKU's function to advise on the luak's customary decisions, as provided for under Article 16 of the state constitution.
He said the DKU heard a complaint at the meeting from the Ibu Soko Klana Hulu and Waris Klana Hulu as representatives of Telaga Undang Luak Sungei Ujong.
Raja Norazli said they had removed Mubarak Dohak as undang of Sungei Ujong according to the luak's customs through a termination letter dated May 13, 2025.

He said that Tuanku Muhriz clearly emphasised that the power to choose, appoint and remove undangs lies with the luak itself under the state constitution. Furthermore, DKU members, including Tuanku Muhriz, have no power to support or reject the luak's decisions.

“As such, the DKU accepted the termination as a decision made by the luak according to its customs under Article 14(3). The DKU did not terminate any undang, nor did Tuanku Muhriz. The DKU accepted the luak's decision to terminate the undang of Sungei Ujong,” Raja Norazli said in a statement today.

On Friday, the four purported undangs of Negeri Sembilan, together with the Tunku Besar of Tampin, defended their bid to remove Tuanku Muhriz as Yang Dipertuan Besar, claiming the ruler had breached provisions of an 1898 agreement.
The chieftains claimed the ruler had breached two clauses in the agreement by interfering in the customary affairs of each area, and entertaining complaints against their appointed undangs.

Raja Norazli said that the 1898 agreement between the Yang Dipertuan Besar and the Undang Yang Empat was an important part of the state’s constitutional history but was no longer the state’s sole source of constitutional rights or powers.

“It must be read subject to the express provisions of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and can only be given effect insofar as it does not conflict with the state constitution,” he said.

Raja Norazli said Article 16(1) of the state constitution also expressly states that the DKU must advise on questions of Malay custom referred to it, and any delay or failure to do so constitutes a neglect of the duty entrusted to it.

“We discussed the prospect of reinstating the Malaysian Grand Prix as a permanent fixture on the F1 calendar, thereby fulfilling the long-standing wishes of fans who have been eagerly awaiting its return to Sepang,” he said in a Facebook post today.

Anwar said the Cabinet would discuss the matter and consider the country’s capability to host the race and how its return would benefit the economy and the people. A Sepang circuit official previously estimated that a permanent place on the F1 calendar would cost Malaysia RM300 million a year.

The prime minister was at Sepang today for the Bahrain Grand Prix, held in Malaysia after the race was initially cancelled because of the US-Iran war. At a trackside interview with F1 commentator Martin Brundle, Anwar said, “Well, I’m looking forward to it. We're discussing”.

The race was won by Max Verstappen of Red Bull, marking his return to Sepang after nine years. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes finished second, while Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton came from 18th place to finish third. Hamilton had previously won at Sepang in 2014 after eight attempts, securing a Mercedes one-two victory with Nico Rosberg.

This weekend's F1 race was the first to be held at Sepang since the Malaysian Grand Prix was cancelled in 2017 after an 18 year run due to rising expenses and declining returns. The cost of the event was borne by Bahrain, while Malaysia spent between RM10 million and RM16 million on preparations.
623e8957d338a5ec: TAIZ: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Sunday cut a vital supply route linking Taiz with Aden - the interim capital of the internationally recognised government - according to four security sources.
The Houthi advance follows days of heavy fighting in and around the city of Taiz between the group and government forces.
"We were informed that the Houthis had taken control of the al-Safiya area, where they cut the main road and took control of the police station," a police source in the area told AFP.
Three sources with the Yemeni military also confirmed Houthi control over the area and supply route, with the group effectively encircling Taiz city.
The military sources added that the Houthis had also halted traffic on the main road linking Taiz to Aden, with fighting in the area ongoing.
The city itself remains under the control of government forces but has long been besieged from the north, east and west by Houthi fighters and remains one of the main fronts in Yemen's civil war.
"They've achieved the military objective of isolating Taiz from Aden, even if they haven't fully taken control of it," Farea Al-Muslimi, research fellow at the Chatham House think-tank, told AFP.
Elsewhere in Yemen, the Houthi's Al-Masirah TV channel reported Saudi strikes in the northern governorates of al-Jawf and Saada, saying at least two people had been wounded.

The strikes come a day after Yemen's government said its forces hit Houthi targets around the country, including in the capital Sanaa, the northwestern governorate of Saada and the group's positions near Taiz in the southwest.
The Yemeni government's air capabilities however remain limited.
Since a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015 in support of the government, it has primarily been Riyadh's forces that have carried out airstrikes against the Houthis.
Experts believe the recent operations have most likely been conducted by Saudi warplanes rather than the Yemeni air force.
Following several years of relative calm, Yemen's war reignited in July against the backdrop of the widening Middle East war.
The country is one of the poorest in the world and remains gripped by a vast humanitarian crisis.
Fighting intensified in September as the Houthis launched a lightning offensive that saw them seize Yemen's entire Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital shipping lane.
The Houthis have in parallel launched a blockade on Saudi energy exports, already squeezed by Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Yemen's war erupted in 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa from the Saudi-backed government, before going on to take control of swaths of the country's north.
Riyadh intervened in the war the following year as the head of the international coalition.
3e96c3f7a949191a: KUALA LUMPUR: TV3's acclaimed documentary series Majalah 3 will air a special one-hour tribute tomorrow night to the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, offering viewers an intimate look into the life of a figure widely cherished as the "mother of the nation."
Broadcast as a final salute, the documentary goes beyond marking her passing.
It explores lesser-known sides of her life as a medical pioneer, dedicated public figure, and devoted wife to former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad.

The tribute brings together heartfelt reflections from close friends and prominent figures, including Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail (wife of the Prime Minister); legendary national badminton player Datuk Rashid Sidek; acclaimed filmmaker and producer Erma Fatima; and Universiti Malaya deputy vice-chancellor Professor Dr Zamri Radzi.

At the heart of the show is Dr Siti Hasmah's genuine warmth and humility toward people from all walks of life. One touching story comes from Siti Masitah Awang Kechik, who often prepared traditional treats for Dr Siti Hasmah—a simple gesture that shows her natural gift for making everyone feel like family.
Dr Wan Azizah reflects on Dr Siti Hasmah's groundbreaking career as one of Malaysia's first female doctors, while Rashid Sidek remembers her deep care for national athletes.
Adding a rare personal touch, Erma Fatima shares charming stories about the lifelong bond between Dr Siti Hasmah and Tun Dr Mahathir.

From personal memories shared by friends and mentees to insights from the arts and sports, every story highlights a woman whose quiet strength was built on strong principles, lifelong sacrifice, and a deep love for her country.
Majalah 3 Istimewa: Tun Dr Siti Hasmah airs on Oct 5 at 9pm on TV3. It will also be available to stream on Tonton.
49b0d01e1efeb479: GERIK: The crash on the Gerak-Jeli stretch of the East-West Highway that killed four, including a child, happened when the Perodua Axia they were travelling in went out of control.
The vehicle entered the opposite lane at Km38.5 of the highway near Tasik Banding and crashed into another car and a lorry.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the Axia was travelling from Gerik towards Jeli when the crash happened about 1.30pm.
He said the vehicle crashed into the rear of a Proton Persona, which was travelling from Jeli towards Gerik.
"Following the collision, the Axia went underneath the lorry and was dragged for about 3m to 7m," he said in a statement.
Alwi said four occupants of the Axia, comprising two men, a woman and a child, were confirmed dead.
"Another child suffered serious injuries and was taken to Gerik Hospital for treatment.
"The Axia was driven by a 19-year-old man and had four passengers comprising a 31-year-old man, a 40-year-old woman and two children.
"The Proton Persona was driven by a 20-year-old man with three passengers – two men aged 19 and 47, and a 47-year-old woman," he said.
He added that the lorry was driven by a 42-year-old man and had a 34-year-old male attendant.
Alwi said the Proton Persona driver and all its passengers, as well as the lorry driver and attendant, were uninjured.
"All three vehicles involved will be sent for technical inspection.
"Police are also tracing independent witnesses and seeking closed-circuit television (CCTV) and dashboard camera (dashcam) recordings, if available, to assist further investigations," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Those with information on the crash are urged to come forward to assist with investigations.
Meanwhile, the identities of the victims have been established, but their relationship has yet to be ascertained.
Gerik police chief Superintendent Abdul Samad Othman said the victims were all from Kota Baru.
They were identified as Al Zubair Deraman, 31; Tuan Shazrin Tuan Mud, 40; and Nik Mohamad Hafiz Daniel Nik Hairey, 19.
He said the identity of the child, a girl, had yet to be ascertained.
The injured victim was identified as Mohammad Shiraz Hammani Abdul Fattah, 9.
