7adcff61d6d7f37c: KUALA LUMPUR: Golongan muda India tidak seharusnya dipersalahkan kerana mempersoalkan sumbangan MIC kepada negara apabila MIC sendiri gagal mendokumentasikan pencapaian pemimpin-pemimpinnya dengan secukupnya, kata Timbalan Presiden MIC M Saravanan.
Saravanan berkata generasi sekarang mungkin generasi terakhir yang mempunyai pengetahuan secara langsung mengenai sumbangan oleh pemimpin-pemimpin MIC terdahulu.

"Jika kita tidak mendokumentasikan semua ini dengan betul dalam tempoh 10 tahun akan datang, sejarah ini akan hilang. Generasi akan datang tidak akan tahu apa yang telah kita lakukan dan sumbangkan," katanya dalam ucapan sempena pelancaran biografi bekas presiden MIC, V Manickavasagam.
Versi bahasa Inggeris dan Tamil biografi 'Tan Sri Manickavasagam: Memories-Reflections-Achievements' dilancarkan hari ini sempena ulang tahun kelahiran ke-100 presiden MIC keenam itu.
Manickavasagam memimpin MIC dari 1973 sehingga kematiannya pada 1979. Beliau berkhidmat dalam Jemaah Menteri tiga perdana menteri -- Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra, Abdul Razak Hussein dan Hussein Onn.
Saravanan berkata pemimpin-pemimpin MIC terdahulu seperti Manickavasagam memainkan peranan penting dalam pembangunan Malaysia, khususnya dalam bidang pengangkutan, telekomunikasi dan prasarana.

Beliau menarik perhatian kepada peranan Manickavasagam dalam membangunkan perlindungan keselamatan sosial yang akhirnya membawa kepada penubuhan Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso), selain peranan VT Sambanthan dalam pembinaan bangunan Parlimen dan Lapangan Terbang Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah di Subang.
Saravanan turut menekankan peranan Manickavasagam dalam penubuhan Malaysian Airline System (MAS) susulan perpisahan Malaysia-Singapore Airlines.
Beliau berkata Manickavasagam menyedari kepentingan pendidikan teknikal dan vokasional untuk masyarakat India beberapa dekad sebelum perkara itu dibincangkan secara meluas.

"Beliau berkata jika kita mahu mengubah masyarakat, ia perlu dilakukan melalui pendidikan," kata Saravanan, dan menambah Manickavasagam memulakan program pendidikan teknikal dan vokasional melalui MIC.

Beliau turut mengetengahkan bagaimana pembinaan ibu pejabat MIC pada 1973 dilakukan tanpa mengambil pinjaman, menyifatkannya sebagai pencapaian penting kepimpinan Manickavasagam yang wajar dipelihara dalam sejarah parti.
19feb8c5dba7662d: NAGOYA, Oct 4 — Japan is traditionally seen as a reliable host for major sporting events but an Asian Games dogged by organisational woes has tarnished that image and raised questions over future bids, experts say.
The Games in Aichi-Nagoya saw a catalogue of mishaps, from athletes bussed to the wrong venues to the North Korean national anthem played for the South Korean hockey team.
There were not enough beds for the over 17,000 athletes and officials, a bigger number than the Olympics.
Countries complained of being stranded for up to six hours at the airport on arrival.
Teams were not shy in criticising the local organisers.
Ryu Seung-min, president of the Korean Sport and Olympic Committee, said: “If I were to give them a grade, it would be an F.”
Japanese Olympic Committee (JOC) president Seiko Hashimoto admitted that “there were many problems”, but said the country wants to host more international events.
Harsh criticism
Hirokazu Arai, a professor specialising in sports psychology, told AFP that Japan may struggle to escape the shadow of the Asian Games for some time to come.
“If Japan were to bid for the Olympics again, trust in Japan may have fallen and it might be harder to win a bid,” he said.
“And within Japan, people may take the view that if these kinds of things are going to happen, we don’t need the Olympics.”
Many in Japan have questioned the value of hosting major sporting events as they grapple with the fallout from the graft-stained and pandemic-delayed Tokyo Olympics.
Cost overruns, corruption and Covid all tainted the public’s memory of the Games, which took place largely behind closed doors in 2021, a year later than planned.
Japan was praised by some, however, for getting the Games on in unprecedented circumstances.
The country subsequently dropped the idea of hosting the Winter Olympics in the northern city of Sapporo because of a lack of public support.
Hashimoto, who also served as president of the Tokyo Olympics organising committee, has said Sapporo’s bid could be revived.
She said the Asian Games had “reaffirmed my belief in the value of hosting international sporting events in our country”.
“We also received harsh criticism because of the challenges we faced — I am fully aware of that,” she said.
“This is all part of the Games, but we need to analyse those issues so we can tackle them for the next future opportunity.”
Like musical chairs
Asian Games organisers were presented with a headache when the number of athletes and officials that was initially expected ballooned by about 2,000.
Unlike at past Games, there was no traditional athletes’ village in a bid to save money.
Participants instead stayed on a cruise ship, in hotel rooms and in temporary wooden huts.
Some teams complained about the wooden units, saying they were too cramped and the beds too short.
After a troubled build-up, organisers hoped the attention would switch to sport when the action got under way.
But still the problems continued, with transport and accommodation difficulties and further mix-ups with anthems and flags.
“It’s like musical chairs,” a Thai official said, adding that organisation at the Games had been “chaotic”.
Nagoya’s mayor apologised to athletes for “inconveniences”, saying organisers would “sincerely reflect on the mishandling that occurred”.
There were sparse crowds at some events, starting with thousands of empty seats at the opening ceremony.
Organisers blamed the bad weather.
Arai believes the Games have damaged Japan’s international reputation as a safe pair of hands.
“The previous Games were in China, and I’m sure there were athletes who came here expecting Japan to put on a better event than China,” he said.
“But I don’t think you can say that’s how it’s turned out.”
Arai says anger that had faded in the years since the Tokyo Olympics could flare up again.
“The people at the top of Japan’s sporting world are moving towards trying to bring the Olympics here again,” he said.
“From their perspective, they may have felt that criticism had started to die down, but this situation could cause that criticism to intensify again.” — AFP
bcd3ee898d3deb93: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 4 — More than 500 adults in Sabah who missed out on formal education are being given a second chance to master basic reading, writing and counting (3M) skills through the Functional Literacy Education Programme (PLF) organised by the Community Development Department (KEMAS).

Sabah KEMAS director Ahmad Fakhrul Azman Muhammad Radzi said the participants are attending 25 classes this year in urban fringe, rural and remote areas across Kudat, Kota Marudu, Kota Belud, Keningau, Tenom, Nabawan, Beluran, Sandakan, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Semporna, Tawau and Kalabakan.
The programme primarily targets individuals aged between 15 and 65 who have yet to master basic 3M skills, while those outside the age range can also participate based on their needs.
“PLF is among the efforts to eradicate illiteracy, particularly among those who dropped out of formal education at an early stage and are still unable to read, write and count,” he told Bernama.

Participants are identified with the help of community leaders, including village heads, as well as KEMAS teachers on the ground, who provide information on individuals still in need of literacy education.

Before joining the classes, participants sit for a pre-test to assess their initial reading, writing and counting skills. A post-test is conducted upon completion to measure their progress, with more than 70 per cent recorded as achieving an excellent level.
Those who have yet to fully master the three skills can repeat the lessons to ensure they reach the required level.
Ahmad Fakhrul said regular PLF classes run for a year and are conducted by KEMAS-appointed PLF community development officers who serve as trained educators in the targeted areas.
Classes conducted by additional instructors in areas with greater needs run for six months, with three sessions a week.
As part of efforts to recognise participants and encourage them to continue learning, graduation ceremonies are held according to class and district.
A total of 375 participants from 25 classes took part in this year’s ceremonies, which were conducted by groups and according to their respective districts.

“Participants who complete the programme receive certificates as recognition and encouragement to continue learning. We do not know whether they may eventually become interested in pursuing further education,” he said.

Beyond literacy, KEMAS instructors also expose participants to livelihood and entrepreneurship skills through the production of items such as handicrafts, fish crackers and rempeyek, based on local needs.
“We want participants to apply their basic 3M skills in small-scale entrepreneurship so that they can indirectly generate income,” said Ahmad Fakhrul.
As technology advances, PLF participants are also introduced to digital skills to help them keep pace with current developments and reduce the digital divide.
They are guided in using smartphones for everyday tasks, including making clinic appointments through the MySejahtera application and paying bills, as well as promoting their products online
“Efforts to eradicate illiteracy must continue and receive support from all parties so that no one, particularly in Sabah, is left behind in education.

“We do not want them to be easily deceived in their daily affairs because of literacy limitations. Instead, they should be supported until they can become independent and live their lives with greater confidence,” he said. — Bernama
f18720085ee79e81: TEHRAN, Oct 4 — Huge billboards on the walls of Tehran mocking US President Donald Trump and depicting American drones under the boot of an Iranian soldier are providing a chronicle of Iran’s war with the United States and Israel.

AFP got rare access to a team producing the billboards with anti-US messaging for prominent locations in Tehran where they are seen daily by large crowds of passers-by, including the city’s famed Valiasr Square.

Khaneh-ye Tarrahan, or Designers’ House, created a towering portrayal of Trump’s lips sewn and his mouth muzzled by the Strait of Hormuz waterway at the centre of the Iran war, accompanied by the words “At the breaking point”.
“When news breaks, the team mobilises: ideas are generated, the graphic designers are briefed and we collaborate,” said Mostafa Kafaei, 32, who manages the studio.
As he spoke, people worked on projects at several desks in the office.
It features a whiteboard for brainstorming, while photos of martyrs and ideas adorn the hallway wall.
Kafaei’s studio, which includes a dedicated media-monitoring team, works under one of the country’s biggest state-run media conglomerates.
The billboards are sponsored by the government and used to convey its messages far and wide.
One from a different studio shows Trump trapped inside a magician’s box, clutching a Coca-Cola and a hamburger with the words: “Blink, you’re gone!”
The billboard references a July incident in Turkey where Trump was smuggled from Air Force One to a different aircraft on a catering truck due to a security threat.
“Speed has become a top priority,” said Kafaei, with urgent posters turned around in just a few days by teams of up to around eight people.
Most of their work is created in Photoshop, he said, adding that the team is “highly proficient in AI”, using “various AI engines, such as ChatGPT and Nano Banana” as part of the production process.
Media war

Another towering billboard recently put up in Tehran shows an Iranian soldier stepping on a US underwater drone, depicting a recent “Hormuz catch” by Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and bragging that “Business is good”.

Iran has blockaded commercial shipping through the Hormuz strait since the war began in late February with US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic, while the US military has upheld a counterblockade of Iran’s ports.
A different advert shows a mythical warrior standing in raging seas as US warships burn, along with a message reading “Satan’s army will drown in the Persian Gulf”.
Riffing off the cover of Nirvana’s “Nevermind” album, another depicts Trump grasping at a dollar bill underwater, next to the words “GREAT VICTORY! Strait of Hormuz”.

“There was some initial hesitation about whether to feature such a large image of Trump’s face on the Valiasr mural,” Kafaei said of the image with Trump’s lips sewn up, which appeared in May as the strategic trade route became central to the conflict.
But “the overall assessment was that the final piece would be exceptionally powerful”, he said.
When asked why the US leader featured on so many billboards, Kafaei said Trump “is a media personality... We respond in kind whenever he takes action in that space”.
Comparing it to a battlefield scenario with an adversary “constantly firing at us”, the studio chief said “we keep a close watch on our opponent and respond accordingly”.
Satan’s wedding gift
Large billboards glorifying Iran, its former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, killed at the start of the war, and allies like slain Hezbollah chief Hassan Nasrallah have also appeared around the city.
Kafaei said the billboards helped many people who “may not be politically minded” to grasp “the overall context of what is going on in the country”.

Retiree Mahmoudreza Rezaei, 53, recalled seeing a billboard that referred to “Satan’s wedding gift” — a message he understood to be directed at Trump after an alleged US attack in the country’s south last month that killed several people at a wedding ceremony.
“It kept me pondering for a few minutes, trying to decipher the meaning,” Rezaei said.
“It had a bit of a riddle-like quality.”
Sahar Jahedi, 24, who works in a pharmacy, said she was captivated by the billboard of Trump trapped in the magician’s box, which went up in central Tehran’s Jomhouri Square.
While “so many people are currently struggling just to survive, they may not have the time” to follow the news, she said.
“Billboards like this... can play a significant role in keeping more people informed about current events.” — AFP
818552f2999a07ee: HOUSTON, Oct 4 — A one-year-old toddler stumbles around an immigration court in Louisiana, crying. He throws a toy that nearly hits a prosecutor.
The judge instructs the baby and his mother, age 17, to apply for asylum. But the teenager can barely focus on what he is saying.
Roxana Avila-Cimpeanu, deputy director of a group that provides legal support for unaccompanied minors, described this scene, which she witnessed in August.

“This child is being expected to file her own application, also figure out how to file things for her one-year-old baby, while living through the distress of being a detained young mother,” Avila-Cimpeanu told AFP.

President Donald Trump’s administration has choked off funding for organisations that have years of experience assisting unaccompanied minors, bringing in substitutes that are under-equipped and unqualified, advocates say.

“We are gravely concerned that ORR would entrust a vulnerable population with firms so plainly unqualified for the task,” Democratic lawmakers said in a letter to the Deportment of Health and Human Services this week.
ORR is the Office of Refugee Resettlement, an agency traditionally tasked with the care of unaccompanied minor migrants.
The category describes children who arrive in the United States without an adult, or whose parents were detained by immigration agents and are in shelters or government custody.
Attack on children

Since he returned to the White House for his second term in January 2025, President Donald Trump has a mounted an aggressive and sometimes violent operation to deport undocumented immigrants from the United States.
Last year the administration tried to cut off funding that ORR used to support a national network of organisations that have for years provided legal services to unaccompanied migrant minors.
Following a lawsuit, the measure was blocked by a federal judge who ordered that the services, which were mandated by a 2008 law, be maintained.
Months later, the government stopped making payments, and in July 2026, it allowed a contract with the Acacia Centre for Justice — which managed a network of about 100 organisations — to expire.

Avila-Cimpeanu told AFP that in late 2025 that the government made funding contingent on the release of confidential information about some 20,000 children represented by the network — “and we did not do so.”
The government then announced plans to hand the cases over to the Burke Law Group, run by a former Trump administration official, but that firm withdrew its bid.
It then planned to deploy Our Rescue, an organisation founded by a controversial anti-trafficking activist and led by a former investigator for Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).
The contract was put on hold following questions raised in Congress, amid a review of federal funds allocated for this purpose.
“Children’s legal protections should never be the currency Of political patronage,” Democratic lawmakers said in their letter.
Avila-Cimpeanu says the administration is trying to complicate the defense of minors “in order to get to their goal of deporting as many children as quickly as possible.”
“I have been doing this work for 10 years, and this is the worst time that I’ve ever seen with regard to the government’s concerted attack on children,” she said.
Babies in court

She said it is common for unaccompanied minors to appear in immigration courts. That is why a lawyer who understands the issue—and even speaks the child’s language if it is not English — is necessary.
Avila-Cimpeanu recalled a case in 2018 when her organisation was in court on behalf of a baby just months old.
“We had to say: this baby denies the allegations. This baby would like voluntary departure.
“It’s ridiculous that children have to go through this process as if they were adults, but it is part of the proceeding.”
This week, CNN reported that 25 migrant children, several without a lawyer, had a hearing in a Texas court.
In a statement to AFP, ORR said that in August it provided funding through the end of the year for the US Committee for Refugees and Immigrants (USCRI) to appear at immigration hearings.
“USCRI is appearing at 100 percent of the hearings and has expanded to provide legal orientation, legal consultations and direct representation,” it said.
Bilal Askaryar, a spokesman for Acacia, explained that USCRI is a small organization with about 50 attorneys, compared to the 800 in Acacia’s network.
“This isn’t about a contract for us. This isn’t about a dispute between an organization and the government. This is about 20,000 children who came to the United States seeking safety,” he said. — AFP
5b350d660c173a07: PARIS, Oct 4 — Protests by teenagers outside their schools have shaken France in recent days, with students blockading entrances to their institutions and security forces on occasion responding with tear gas.
The government has said that while the grievances may be legitimate, violence is not and has accused the hard-left of whipping up the movement.
Critics have meanwhile accused some police of heavy-handed force against protesters, who are legally still children.
More than 5,000 people have been arrested since Monday, according to the interior ministry, while about 735 educational establishments were affected on Friday, the education minister said.
While the weekend may see a lull, a major new day of protest is planned for Tuesday.
AFP looks at the origins of the movement.
Multiple grievances
The protests affect lycees, the schools where French teens have their last years of school aged from 15–18, the equivalent of high school in the United States and sixth form in the United Kingdom.

The students’ grievances are numerous, but chief among them are teacher absences, conditions in classrooms, overloaded school timetables and a school day that can be as long as 8am to 6pm, which some say is excessive.
“High-school students — particularly those from low-income neighbourhoods — feel they are receiving an inferior education,” said French sociologist Valerie Becquet.
Origin of the movement
The movement began two weeks ago on September 17 at the Saint-Exupery high school in the Paris suburb of Creteil, in support of teachers striking over a lack of staff and resources.
It gained momentum, gradually spreading across the country over the last week.

Ironically, as tensions raged elsewhere in France, the situation at the Saint-Exupery high school returned to normal after educational authorities agreed to send additional staff, including a deputy principal and a nurse.

“Our grades were slipping. If we had not rallied now it would have augured very badly for the future,” said pupil Abderrahmane, who expressed “enormous” pride at taking part in the inception of the movement.
Role of social media
The protests are being further fuelled by the spread of dramatic images and videos on online platforms, notably TikTok.

Students themselves hold up their phones to record scenes such as burning trash cans or police deploying tear gas. Numerous channels, seeking to boost their reach, spread this footage and edit together the most dramatic moments.
“With social media, they can offer a narrative different from the one presented in traditional media — a narrative that is not manufactured,” said sociologist Becquet.
Social inequality
France offers all students access to the lycee but in reality there is a vast spectrum, ranging from vocational schools to elite institutions.
Despite numerous diversity initiatives, the latter remain dominated by students from white, affluent families with university-educated parents.
“There are glaring inequalities among different students and schools, and this is a real problem,” said Becquet.
Political exploitation

The protests have become a major issue of political tension just over half a year ahead of presidential elections with the government accusing the hard left France Unbowed (LFI) of being behind the movement.
Senior LFI official Manuel Bompard has rejected the government’s accusations, saying it was “descending into conspiracy theories”.

Veteran LFI presidential candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon — who is currently polling at over 40 per cent among 18-25-year-old voters — has strongly supported the protests, while calling for non-violent methods.
Police response
Protesters have blockaded schools, set fire to bins and other objects and hurled projectiles at police.
But police have also moved to disperse some of the protesters, notably firing tear gas canisters, using rubber bullets and sometimes beating them with batons.
After students clashed with police Wednesday in Tours in central France, one young man wounded lost the use of his right eye, the city’s prosecutor said.
Numerous videos have gone viral showing alleged brutal conduct by security forces — such as a police officer placing his arm around the neck of a girl during her arrest.
But police have also been targets, notably an officer who was chased and beaten and kicked by a group of youths from a school in the eastern city of Belfort. — AFP

61b28548f7c8ca41: PETALING JAYA: Commercial considerations regarding the operations of Petronas cannot override Sarawak’s constitutional rights, a senator form Sarawak said today to rebut a contention by former law minister Zaid Ibrahim.
Senator Ahmad Ibrahim of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu said the amount of money involved could not decide who had legal authority over the state’s oil and gas sector.

“If a constitutional or legal right exists, it does not disappear merely because recognising it may affect another entity’s revenue,” he was quoted by Dayak Daily as saying today, in response to Zaid's contention that Petronas would lose key business operations when Sarawak's oil company Petros takes over from Petronas as the state gas aggregator.

Zaid had disputed an assurance by Sarawak premier Abang Johari Openg that Petros will not displace or undermine Petronas. Zaid said Petronas stood to lose billions if it lost control of its gas aggregation role.

Ahmad disputed the figure of RM10 billion a year for the gas business; he said the figure represented broader profit estimates from Sarawak’s gas exports, rather than confirmed losses that Petronas would suffer.

Ahmad pushed back against claims that the current arrangement forces Petronas to forfeit its status as the national petroleum company. He said Sarawak’s laws, such as the Oil Mining Ordinance 1958, predated the formation of Malaysia in 1963 and the enactment of the Petroleum Development Act in 1974.

He said a joint declaration signed by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Abang Johari on May 21 last year established a framework in which federal and state laws coexist. "This should not become a contest of Petronas versus Petros, much less Malaysia versus Sarawak. A mature federation should be capable of doing both,” he said.
b14d946d6bebd375: ISLAMABAD: Talks between Pakistan's government and the party of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan aimed at avoiding a major demonstration stalled on Sunday, with supporters vowing to go ahead with their protest.

Authorities have been preparing for weeks for the possible arrival of demonstrators in Islamabad, with the march planned by supporters of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party originally slated for Sept 27 and then postponed until Sunday.
Sohail Afridi, the chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which is ruled by the PTI, posted on X early on Sunday that the "long march" in support of Khan would go ahead.
Discontent over Khan's incarceration has mounted in recent months, particularly over the 73-year-old's medical treatment and access to him by doctors and family.
The PTI has also called for the release of Khan's three sisters, whose arrests last month further heightened tensions.
Opposition politician Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said last-minute talks between the government and representatives from PTI were in "deadlock".
Abbas told Geo TV, a popular private news channel, that negotiators had hit an impasse over demands that included access to Khan by his doctor.

Khan, a hugely popular former cricket star, has been behind bars since August 2023 and faces scores of charges, ranging from corruption to treason and inciting violence, following widespread anti-establishment riots in May 2023.
He and his legal team reject the allegations, branding them as politically motivated cases aimed at neutralising his popularity.
Afridi said the demonstration was to begin in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on Sunday and make its way to Khairabad, 80km west of Islamabad, by Thursday.
Further phases of the plan would be announced in Khairabad, the provincial chief minister said, without specifying when demonstrators could arrive in the Pakistani capital.
Authorities in Islamabad have blocked main access routes to the capital with double-stacked shipping containers in preparation for the protest, obstructing traffic and public transit.
The Supreme Court ruled in August that Khan should be moved to a civilian hospital for treatment, but authorities instead returned him to prison after a short stay at a government-run hospital.
9631a47d4053d789: KOTA BARU: Local councils in the state have captured 36 stray dogs this year, with most of the animals rounded up in Bachok, including the Kemasin area where an 8-year-old boy was recently attacked.
State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the operations were carried out between January and last week.
"The local authorities had intensified efforts to address the stray dog problem, particularly in areas where such animals had been reported to pose a threat to the public.
"As of October, 36 stray dogs have been captured.
"Most of them were caught in Bachok, including Kemasin and other surrounding areas.
"Some of the dogs were captured while the rest had entered the traps," he said.
The 8-year-old boy was injured after being attacked by more than five stray dogs while playing at Pantai Kuala Kemasin in Bachok on Thursday.
The boy sustained injuries to his head, neck and hand in the incident and underwent surgery to treat his wounds.
It was reported today that the boy will also be given anti-rabies injections to prevent infection.
His mother, Rosnani Mat Salleh, 46, said the vaccination was part of a multi-week follow-up treatment plan for her son, Azuar Firdaus Zuraiman, following a five-hour surgery yesterday.
58270372799eed6c: MOTEGI: Defending world champion Marc Marquez won the Japanese MotoGP on Sunday to slice Jorge Martin's overall championship lead to two points with six events of the season remaining.
Marquez pushed pole-sitter Martin into second place in Motegi after overtaking his fellow Spaniard midway through the race.
It put seven-time world champion Marquez back within touching distance of the championship lead after losing ground in the previous race in Austria.
Marquez completed the double after also winning Saturday's sprint race in Japan.
He said it was "very important" to claim maximum points from the weekend.
"The race was tough, especially when I was behind Jorge, but I knew that if I was able to lead the race the pace was good," he said.
"Jorge tried to attack but then I just increased the pace and it was enough to do the last two laps more relaxed."
Italian Marco Bezzecchi finished third and slipped further behind in the title race.
Marquez dropped to the tarmac to fire off a round of press-ups before the race in a new warm-up routine.
The Ducati rider then flexed his muscles on his bike, biding his time behind Martin before making his move in lap 11.
Martin said he had "a good package to fight for the rest of the season" but admitted that Marquez was the better rider on the day.
"I think today to win was really difficult," said Martin.
"It was one of the days when I rode almost perfectly, I was really smooth, really confident, and even then I couldn't win."
It was Marquez's sixth grand prix win of the season, despite missing the races in Le Mans and Catalonia to undergo surgery on his foot and shoulder.
A sunny day in Japan clouded over and cooled considerably shortly before the race but the rain held off.
Marquez never looked in any trouble once he had gone past Martin, who in turn looked comfortable in second place.
Bezzecchi had to fight a furious rearguard action to hold off fellow Italia Enea Bastianini, who finished fourth.
Spain's Pedro Acosta, who chalked up his first ever victory in MotoGP in Austria, finished seventh.
Ai Ogura, who was bidding to become the first Japanese race winner in Motegi since 2004, was sixth.
Brazil's Diogo Moreira, who finished second in the sprint when Martin was demoted to third due to a penalty, crashed out of the grand prix.--AFP

0fdf8126923da165: BATU PAHAT: The Form Four pupil who was believed to have been murdered at a school in Yong Peng was laid to rest at the Kampung Parit Arshad Muslim cemetery, here.

Earlier, the 16-year-old suspect who was detained at 7pm yesterday was remanded for six days by the Batu Pahat magistrate's court.

21e12596eaae6c1a: PETALING JAYA: Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) Negeri Sembilan menyangkal dakwaan bahawa Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir mencampuri urusan Luak Sungei Ujong dalam suatu sidang pada 17 April tahun ini.

Setiausaha DKU Raja Norazli Raja Nordin berkata sidang itu merupakan DKU menjalankan fungsinya sebagaimana yang dikehendaki oleh Perkara 16 UUTKNS, iaitu menerima dan memberi nasihat berhubung keputusan yang telah pun dibuat oleh Luak menurut adat.
Tuanku Muhriz adalah Yang Dipertua Dewan pada sidang tersebut.
Menurut Raja Norazli, perkara yang dibawa ke hadapan DKU pada sidang itu ialah aduan yang dibuat oleh wakil-wakil Telaga Undang Luak Sungei Ujong, iaitu Ibu Soko dan Waris Klana Hulu.
Menurutnya, mereka telah memberhentikan Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak daripada jawatan Undang menurut adat Luak tersebut, melalui surat pemberhentian yang diserahkan pada 13 Mei 2025.

Raja Norazli berkata Tuanku Muhriz dengan jelas menegaskan bahawa kuasa adat untuk memilih, melantik dan memberhentikan Undang terletak pada Luak itu sendiri bawah Perkara 14(1) dan (3), dan ahli Dewan, termasuk Yang Dipertua Dewan sendiri, tidak mempunyai kuasa untuk menyokong atau menolak keputusan Luak sedemikian.
"Oleh itu, Dewan menerima pemberhentian tersebut sebagai pemberhentian yang dibuat oleh Luak menurut adatnya sendiri, di bawah Perkara 14(3)," katanya dalam kenyataan.
"Dewan tidak memberhentikan mana-mana Undang. Tuanku Muhriz juga tidak berbuat demikian. Dewan menerima keputusan yang telah dibuat oleh Luak untuk memberhentikan Undang Luak Sungei Ujong," katanya.

Pada 2 Okt lalu, empat individu yang mendakwa sebagai Undang Negeri Sembilan, bersama Tunku Besar Tampin, mendakwa Tuanku Muhriz melanggar dua fasal dalam Perjanjian 1898 kerana campur tangan dalam hal ehwal adat di luak, selain melayan aduan terhadap Undang.
Dengan mendakwa Tuanku Muhriz melanggar peruntukan Perjanjian 1898, kumpulan tersebut mempertahankan tindakan mereka menurunkan baginda sebagai Yang Dipertuan Besar.
Raja Norazli berkata perjanjian bertarikh 29 April 1898 antara Yang Dipertuan Besar dengan Undang Yang Empat merupakan sebahagian penting daripada sejarah perlembagaan Negeri Sembilan.
Bagaimanapun, Raja Norazli menerangkan bahawa perjanjian itu tidak lagi terpakai sebagai sumber tunggal bagi hak atau kuasa perlembagaan.
"Ia mesti dibaca tertakluk kepada peruntukan nyata UUTKNS dan hanya boleh diberi kesan setakat mana ia tidak bercanggah dengan UUTKNS," katanya.

Raja Norazli berkata Perkara 16(1) UUTKNS memperuntukkan secara nyata bahawa DKU hendaklah memberi nasihat mengenai persoalan adat Melayu yang dirujuk kepadanya, dan kegagalan atau kelewatan berbuat demikian merupakan satu pengabaian terhadap tugas yang diamanahkan.
"Tiada dokumen sejarah boleh dipetik secara terpilih untuk mengatasi syarat-syarat bertulis Perkara 10," katanya.
51c491e8434ddf77: SEPANG, Oct 4 — Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team’s Kimi Antonelli admitted second place was the maximum the team could achieve in the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here today.

The current drivers’ standings leader said the Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026 champion Max Verstappen proved too quick as the Red Bull Racing driver claimed his maiden title of the season after a rain-hit and action-packed race in the iconic Malaysian circuit.

Antonelli said the Silver Arrows struggled to match Red Bull Racing’s pace throughout the weekend, while the rough track surface and high temperatures here also made it difficult for the team to assess its new package.
“I think we’re still trying to understand the new package because this track, with such a rough tarmac and high temperatures, made our life more difficult.

“Probably, you know, next week in Singapore GP (Oct 9-11) we hopefully will have a better read on the package, also understanding what setup needs to be run, but I think today with the pace we had, P2 (second place) was the maximum we could have achieved,” he told a post-race press conference.
Previously, the Brackley-based team in the United Kingdom brought an updated front wing and several components to improve local load and the rear corner, among others, to the Canadian GP last May.
It was reported that Mercedes brought its next major upgrade to the Bahrain GP in Malaysia as it looked to strengthen its performance against its rivals this season.

Meanwhile, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who completed the podium in third place, said his decision to start on soft tyres initially appeared to have put his race in jeopardy, but he chose to stay out and wait for the circuit to dry before recovering places during the race.
Hamilton said the team’s decision to stick to the strategy eventually paid off as conditions improved, while strong pit stops also helped him fight his way back into contention.
“Once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great, then after that, really good pit stops from my guys in the garage and good strategy.
“So, for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case, but of course, I’m really, really grateful that we managed to get back here,” he said.
The seven-time world champion said Ferrari still had areas to improve but praised the team for its efforts throughout the weekend.
Today’s result saw Antonelli remain at the top of the drivers’ standings with 320 points, ahead of his teammate George Russell with 236 points, followed by Hamilton in third with 214 points.

Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, who finished fourth today, is in fourth position with 191 points, while reigning world champion Lando Norris of McLaren and Verstappen have 188 points each, in fifth and sixth positions respectively.

In July, Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as the host of the Gulf Air Bahrain GP from October 2 to 4, following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) and the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain.
The agreement kept the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race was cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Malaysia hosted the Malaysian GP at SIC from 1999 to 2017 before the race was dropped from the F1 calendar. — Bernama
e597c10fde25422a: SEPANG: Lewis Hamilton said he had mixed emotions after the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia where he started second on the grid but dropped to 18th when a tyre gamble went wrong before fighting to finish third in a chaotic, rain-hit race on Sunday.
After rain delayed the start of the race by more than 90 minutes, Hamilton was one of the few drivers who switched from intermediate tyres to slicks on a track that was still drying.
The Briton had a slow start and then found himself going backwards, falling as low as 18th, but he opted to stick with his strategy despite Ferrari calling him back into the pits for a tyre change.

Hamilton then carved his way through the field as the track dried up while safety cars also came to his rescue, with the veteran eventually overtaking Red Bull's Isack Hadjar in the dying stages to secure a podium behind Max Verstappen and Kimi Antonelli.

"As a team, we ended up taking that soft (tyre) and at the end of the pit lane, these two (Verstappen and Antonelli) took off their (tyre) blankets and my heart just sank, because I knew straight away that we were in trouble," Hamilton told reporters.
"As we pulled out, all the spray came out the back of Max's car and I was like, 'Okay, I'm done. My race is really in trouble'.
"We made the decision to live with it. As everyone was overtaking me, they (Ferrari) said, 'Should we stop?' I said, 'No, we've already waited another 26 seconds. What's the difference'".

But as the track dried and safety car deployments played into his hands, Hamilton began a remarkable recovery drive as he gave Hadjar chase for fourth place, before George Russell's retirement gave him a shot at a podium.
"I just waited for the track to dry and once it did, it felt good that I was catching people. The car felt great. Then after that, really good pit stops from my guys in the garage," Hamilton added.
"And then a good strategy. So for us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that's what was going to be the case. I'm really, really grateful," he said.
His teammate Charles Leclerc also salvaged fourth place for Ferrari and he conceded that was the best they could have achieved considering how much faster Red Bull and Mercedes were.
"Honestly, the first part of the race, everything that could have gone wrong went wrong. And on the second part, everything that could have gone right went our way," Leclerc said.

"So at the end of the day, I prefer it that way than the other way around. We were P4 today and I honestly think that with a normal race we would have finished P3 and P4. The two guys in front were just way too quick for us.
"Lewis had quite a good pace. I struggled a lot with the car, which we're looking into.
"I had a good feeling on Friday, good feeling until Q2, and then Q3 I started to lose out. Today the race was very tricky," he said.

2b3a585d6fe55bf8: SHAH ALAM: Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) has been urged to set up a department on quantum technology next year to ensure the country does not lag behind current advancements.

The call came from deputy prime minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who said that while artificial intelligence is being implemented "very well", quantum technology represents the latest technological developments, and Malaysia should not lag behind.
Zahid said that he was confident Malaysia could produce quantum technology experts within 10 years.

e37f1b504ed2b0ac: MERCEDES-Benz Malaysia has brought two very different interpretations of high-performance motoring to the local market with the new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé and a preview of the all-new AMG GT 63 four-door coupé.

Unveiled as Formula 1 returns to Malaysia this week, the two models showcase AMG's approach to performance at opposite ends of the powertrain spectrum - one centred on a 4.0-litre V8 biturbo engine and the other on an all-electric AMG.EA architecture.
The GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé is priced from an estimated RM2.09 million in Peninsular Malaysia, while the limited Motorsport Collectors Edition is priced at RM2.59 million.

Mercedes-Benz Cars Malaysia chief executive officer and president, and head of region for Mercedes-Benz Cars Southeast Asia Martin Schulz said the two models reflected AMG's focus on combining performance with emotion.

"The new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 Pro 4Matic+ Coupé brings the thrill of motorsport to the road … while the all-new Mercedes-AMG GT 63 four-door coupé shows how that same spirit can be reimagined for the electric era," he said.
V8 Power, Track-Focused Hardware
The GT 63 Pro is powered by AMG's 4.0-litre V8 biturbo engine producing 450 kW, or 612 hp, and 850 Nm of torque.
That represents a 20 kW increase in output and 50 Nm more torque than the standard AMG GT 63.
Power is sent through AMG's Speedshift MCT 9G transmission and fully variable AMG Performance 4Matic+ all-wheel drive.
The coupé can accelerate from zero to 100 km/h in 3.2 seconds and reach a top speed of 317 km/h. It takes just 10.9 seconds to reach 200 km/h.
AMG has also concentrated on keeping the car cool under sustained track use.
The cooling package has been expanded with additional radiators positioned in the front wheel arches, while the differentials and transfer case also receive active cooling.
Revised underbody air guides and brake cooling ducts help direct more air towards the braking system.
More Grip, Less Lift
The GT 63 Pro also gets extensive aerodynamic changes designed to improve stability and steering precision at high speeds.
Its redesigned front apron features carbon-fibre air deflectors, while active aerodynamic elements in the underbody work with an Airpanel system and a fixed rear wing.
Mercedes-AMG says these changes reduce front-axle aerodynamic lift by more than 30kg, while the rear wing increases rear-axle downforce by about 15kg.
The car rides on AMG Active Ride Control suspension with active roll stabilisation, while rear-axle steering can provide up to 2.5 degrees of steering angle.
Braking duties are handled by AMG ceramic high-performance composite brakes with 420mm discs and six-piston fixed callipers at the front.
The package is designed to withstand repeated heavy braking while reducing unsprung weight.
Carbon-Fibre ameets Luxury
Inside, the GT 63 Pro combines motorsport-inspired equipment with luxury-car technology.
The cabin features AMG Performance seats in Nappa leather and Microcut microfibre, a carbon-fibre/Microcut steering wheel, carbon-fibre trim and yellow seat belts.
A 12.3-inch driver display sits alongside an 11.9-inch central display, with a head-up display and augmented-reality navigation.

AMG Track Pace provides lap, sector and acceleration data for closed-course driving, while the equipment list also includes the Energising Package, Thermotronic automatic climate control and Burmester surround sound.
200 Units Limit
For collectors, Mercedes-AMG is offering a Motorsport Collectors Edition limited to just 200 units globally.
Based on the GT 63 Pro, the special edition features an Obsidian Black finish with Mercedes-Benz Star Pattern graphics and Petronas-coloured exterior accents inspired by Formula 1.
It also features 21-inch forged wheels, carbon-fibre and AMG Night Package elements, Petronas-accented brake callipers and an AMG aerodynamic package.
The cabin receives matching Petronas detailing, AMG Performance seats, carbon-fibre trim and an edition-specific centre-console badge.
The model also comes with a Burmester high-end 3D surround sound system and the Energising Plus Package.
AMG's Electric Flagship
While the GT 63 Pro celebrates the V8, the all-new AMG GT 63 four-door coupé points to the brand's electric future.
The four-door model is based on AMG.EA, a dedicated high-performance electric vehicle architecture, and uses three axial-flux electric motors.
Combined output is up to 860 kW, or 1,169 hp.
The drivetrain is paired with AMG's high performance electric battery, which uses cylindrical cells with direct cooling and an 800-volt electrical architecture.
The setup is designed not only to deliver high peak output but also to sustain performance under repeated high-load conditions.
The car supports DC charging of up to 350 kW, with battery pre-conditioning and thermal management designed to maintain charging performance.
Simulated V8, Electric Performance
AMG has also taken an unusual approach to the electric car's sound and driving character.
Its AMGForce S+ drive programme is designed to provide a V8-inspired experience through simulated gear shifts, sounds and driver-display changes.
The system uses more than 1,600 sound files to create a dynamic acoustic experience that responds to acceleration, gear-change simulations and other driving inputs.
Underneath, the AMG Race Engineer system integrates control of the powertrain, charging, energy management and driving dynamics.
Three rotary controls allow the driver to adjust response, agility and traction characteristics.
The traction control system offers nine levels of adjustment in the appropriate performance modes.
Built For Corners
The GT 63 four-door coupé gets AMG Active Ride Control air suspension with semi-active roll stabilisation, while multi-link front and rear axles maintain wheel control during high-speed cornering.
Active rear-axle steering can turn the rear wheels in the opposite direction to the front wheels at lower speeds to improve agility.
Above 80 km/h, the rear wheels turn in the same direction as the front wheels to improve high-speed stability.
AMG Performance 4Matic+ all-wheel drive provides continuously variable torque distribution between the front and rear axles, with torque vectoring between the rear wheels.
Performance Meets Everyday Use
Despite its performance focus, the four-door model is designed to retain the practicality expected of a grand tourer.
The cabin features AMG Performance seats, Nappa leather and Microcut upholstery, carbon-fibre trim and a panoramic Sky Control roof.
The dashboard combines a 10.2-inch instrument cluster with a 14-inch central display, while the front passenger gets a separate 14-inch screen.
Other equipment includes smartphone integration, augmented-reality navigation and a selfie and video camera.

The two cars offer markedly different routes to AMG performance - the GT 63 Pro leaning heavily on traditional V8 power and track-focused hardware, while the GT 63 four-door coupé demonstrates how AMG is translating its performance philosophy into the electric era.

6a6ab24ef0a6f0c5: KUALA LUMPUR: Indian youths should not be blamed for questioning MIC’s contributions to the nation when it is the party which has failed to adequately document the achievements of its past leaders, says deputy president M Saravanan.
Saravanan said the current generation may be the last to have firsthand knowledge of the contributions made by the party’s former leaders.

“If we do not properly document all this within the next 10 years, this history will be lost. The next generation will not know what we have done and contributed,” he said in a speech at the launch of a biography on former MIC president V Manickavasagam here today.
English and Tamil versions of the biography “Tan Sri Manickavasagam: Memories-Reflections-Achievements” were launched today to mark the centenary of the sixth MIC president’s birth.

Manickavasagam led the party from 1973 until his death in 1979 and served in the Cabinets of Malaysia’s first three prime ministers – Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj, Abdul Razak Hussein and Hussein Onn.
Saravanan said former MIC leaders like Manickavasagam played significant roles in Malaysia’s development, particularly in transportation, telecommunications and infrastructure.

He cited Manickavasagam's role in developing social security protection, which eventually led to the establishment of the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), as well as the late VT Sambanthan’s role in the development of the Parliament building and Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang.
Saravanan also highlighted Manickavasagam's role in the establishment of Malaysian Airline System (MAS) following the break up of Malaysia-Singapore Airlines.
He said Manickavasagam recognised the importance of technical and vocational education for the Indian community decades before it became widely discussed.
“He said that if we want to change society, it has to be done through education,” Saravanan said, adding that Manickavasagam initiated technical and vocational education programmes through MIC.

He also highlighted how the construction of the MIC headquarters in 1973 was done without taking loans, describing it as another significant achievement of Manickavasagam's leadership that should be preserved in the party’s history.

dbb370a9692dbbae: SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un oversaw the launch of a missile which allegedly used artificial intelligence (AI) to adjust its trajectory, state media reported on Sunday.
The AI technology means the missile is "capable of changing its flight orbit at a low altitude", Kim's powerful sister had said, adding this meant there was "no way to avoid" an attack.
"It launched from an area around the eastern coastal city of Wonsan early Saturday morning and flew more than 700km," South Korea's military said.

"Through today's launching drill, the strategic missile soldiers have fully demonstrated their professional qualifications and counterattack posture," Kim said after the launch, according to an English-language dispatch by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).
"We must continue our responsible efforts nonstop to constantly and repeatedly make the enemy recognize the reliability and fatality of our strategic offensive means," he added.
Seoul's military disputed Kim's sister's remarks that there would be "no way to avoid" the projectile guided by AI, saying the missile launched on Saturday could have been intercepted.

"South Korea and the US maintain a firm combined defence posture and assess that the missile recently launched by North Korea was well within the detection and interception capabilities of the defensive assets operated by the two allies," Seoul's defence ministry said in a statement.
"We urge North Korea to immediately cease actions that heighten tensions on the Korean Peninsula," it said, adding that the launch violated UN Security Council resolutions.
The KCNA report disclosed the exact coordinates where the missile hit its target, a level of detail analysts said reflected Pyongyang's "confidence".
"This time, the North disclosed the coordinates down to decimal points - equivalent to a precision of roughly 30cm," Hong Min of the Korea Institute for National Unification told AFP.
"It shows Kim's stance that there is nothing to hide and an expression of confidence," Hong Min said.
Photos released by KCNA showed a missile soaring into the sky in a burst of orange flame.
Another photo showed Kim smiling, flanked by his daughter Ju Ae and wife Ri Sol Ju, who is seen clapping her hands in celebration.

Ju Ae, who was first introduced to the public in 2022, is the most likely successor to her father, according to South Korea's spy agency, citing her increasingly prominent role at major state and military events.
The launch was conducted to help train soldiers operating the "hypersonic strategic weapon system", KCNA reported.

4182c034d30478b8: BRASÍLIA, Oct 4 — Brazilians headed to the polls today in a toss-up race between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro that will decide whether Latin America’s biggest nation follows a regional swing to the right championed by US President Donald Trump.

From villages deep in the Amazon rainforest to the agricultural heartlands in the south and sprawling urban favelas, Brazilians are facing a familiar cast -- with many forced to pick who they least dislike.
Soon to turn 81 years old, the veteran leftist Lula is seeking a fourth and final term in office, warning voters that Brazil’s sovereignty is at stake due to pressure from Trump.

“I am very worried because I want a victory. I can’t understand poor people who are right-wing, because we are naturally left-wing people,” Maria de Nazare Azevedo, a 57-year-old civil servant, told AFP.
“We are poor, we are Northeasterners. Poor right-wingers drive me crazy,” said Azevedo, who lives in Rio de Janeiro but hails from the Amazonian city of Belem.
Bolsonaro leads in the south, among wealthier voters and evangelicals.

“What we need is change, to change politics, to change our security situation. There have been a lot of robberies where I work, and I’ve witnessed various incidents,” said Bolsonaro supporter Babiliana Figueira, 40, a civilian firefighter.
Both candidates have extremely high rejection rates in the deeply polarized nation where a bitter election campaign featured more scandals and mud-slinging than policy and promises.
Lula has slammed Bolsonaro as a “nobody” who is “not even fit to be a building manager.”
Bolsonaro, who has cast himself as more “moderate” said Brazilians “can’t stand” Lula anymore.
‘More enemies’

Lula, revered for social welfare programmes that lifted millions out of poverty, made a dramatic comeback to office in the 2022 elections after a massive corruption scandal that saw him jailed for over 18 months.
The charges, thrown out on procedural grounds, have continued to haunt him.
He beat Jair Bolsonaro in 2022 by only 1.8 per centage points.
Riots in Brasilia and the botched coup attempt after his election allowed him to cast himself as guardian of Brazil’s democracy, even as Jair Bolsonaro’s trial and conviction only deepened divisions.
In his third term he has overseen a drop in inflation and unemployment, but voters complain about a high cost of living and are fed up with crime.
Lula has also sharply curbed deforestation in the Amazon, but the environment has barely registered as a campaign issue.
Indigenous chief Bepdjo Mekragnotire, 45, of the Bau village in the Amazon, told AFP ahead of the vote: “We stand with Lula, all of us.”
“Our concern is that if Flavio wins, there will be more enemies -- more illegal mining, more logging,” he said.
The Trump factor
Trump has loomed large over the campaign, and said he is “very closely” watching the election, but he has not endorsed Flavio Bolsonaro.
The US president has wielded tariffs and sanctions to pressure Brasilia over complaints ranging from the trial against his ally Jair Bolsonaro to alleged unfair trade practices.
Lula has repeatedly warned him not to “meddle” in the elections.
Flavio Bolsonaro’s rallies have featured massive US flags and images of Trump.

Buoyed by his father’s legacy, he has been a formidable rival for Lula, even as it emerged that he was under investigation for corruption over the financing of the biopic “Dark Horse” about his father.
The younger Bolsonaro has vowed a hardline approach to crime and fiscal austerity amid rising public debt.
Carlos Roberto dos Santos, 62, a cattle rancher in the southeastern city of Barretos who supports Bolsonaro, told AFP he was fed up with unchecked government spending.
“They have so many social programmes. To pay off the debt they have to raise interest rates and create new taxes. That affects every sector, not just agriculture.” — AFP

e97a1b2a8d6545f4: SEPANG, Oct 4 — The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) must be prepared to respond to unexpected disruptions — including geopolitical instability — through risk management and assessment, said its president, Mohammed Ben Sulayem.

05c4aa8139f363f6: In 1942, Isaac Asimov formulated three laws of robotics. 58 years later, Jef Raskin responded with three laws of human-computer interface design. They haven’t been bettered yet. There are rules, and even laws, about designing computer user interfaces. Even after 35 years of Linux, which has brought Unix to the masses, the FOSS world has not yet really grasped this. In the meantime, the proprietary software world is busily forgetting everything it once knew. Sometimes these rules surface today, and the FOSS folks often get very cross when reminded that they’re user-interface scofflaws. Marcin Wichary’s recent blog post, They had no concept of a duty of care to their users, is an excellent recent example. (The Reg FOSS desk much admires Mr Wichary’s writing, to the extent that we bought his history of the keyboard, Shift Happens.) In his latest post, Wichary refers to CHERI Project boffin David Chisnall. Chisnall is a long-term Vim user – we all have our failings – and recently recounted trying NeoVim. He uses Vim’s persistent-undo feature, which records changes in a separate directory, so that you can repeatedly undo until you get back to changes you made weeks or months earlier. He’s customized where it’s kept, and when he tried the NeoVim fork, it overwrote his Vim undo file. In a later update to his post, he acknowledges that there was a warning, but he expected it to be safe. It was not safe. It overwrote records of more than a decade’s worth of changes. As he puts it: “Vim has kept this working across major version upgrades over a period of about 20 years. I don’t even think about it, it’s just part of Raskin’s First Law: A program may not harm a user’s data or, through inaction, allow a user’s data to come to harm. If vim or the computer crash, or if I close a file and come back to it six months later, my undo history is still there.” Wichary expands Chisnall’s citation of Raskin’s first law by giving all three, but just in case you’re not a follower of “Golden Age” science fiction, a little context. Asimov introduced his three laws in a short story called “Runaround”, in Astounding Science Fiction magazine* in May 1942. (The story was later collected in the anthology I, Robot – which is nothing like the terrible 2004 film.) A robot may not injure a human being or, through inaction, allow a human being to come to harm. A robot must obey the orders given it by human beings except where such orders would conflict with the First Law. A robot must protect its own existence as long as such protection does not conflict with the First or Second Law. Asimov’s idea was that by setting these rules, he could end the terrible genre of killer-robot stories that was already tired and stale by 1942. Jef Raskin, the lead designer of Apple’s original Macintosh project, attempted to bring similar clarity to software UI. Raskin’s three laws are: A computer shall not harm your work or, through inaction, allow your work to come to harm. A computer shall not waste your time or require you to do more work than is strictly necessary. An interface is humane if it is responsive to human needs and considerate of human frailties. He defined them in his 2000 book The Humane Interface, which you can still buy, or borrow from the Internet Archive. Sadly, Raskin died in 2005, but we have written about his work and his influence several times. He did set some of the direction of the original Macintosh. After Steve Jobs was booted off the Lisa, he took over the Macintosh – as described in The Canon Cat and the Mac that Steve Jobs killed. Raskin quit, and instead designed the remarkable Canon Cat, as we described a couple of years ago. We suspect Raskin was not a fan of Vi, the forerunner of Vim. We aren’t either, which is why we chose the year in the headline of this story: it’s the year Bill Joy wrote vi. Raskin criticized modal software, which requires extra mental effort from the user. So did another UI pioneer, the late great Larry Tesler, who invented the cut/copy/paste trio of commands. Tesler was known for his dictum “Don’t mode me in!” and even had a car license plate reading “NOMODES.” Dr Chisnall has some history of upsetting Unix fans – we’ve referred to one of his papers before: in 2018, he wrote C Is Not a Low-level Language: Your computer is not a fast PDP-11. Unix fans really didn’t like this. This vulture has been told to kill himself for daring to criticize C before now. (We wish we were joking, but no.) Although he has now updated his Mastodon post, the NeoVim fans are not happy. Indeed, one has lambasted this vulture on Bluesky for sharing Wichary’s post. It is interesting to note that NeoVim is the recommended editor in Omarchy, and until recently, the NeoVim developers cited a tweet from DHH on the project website. After an acromonious debate, the pull-quote was removed right around the time of Chisnall’s and Wichary’s posts. In the wide world of software design, we don’t expect the right-wing edge of that community to innovate much in ease of use. In a way, Unix and C embody a machismo infused school of software design: that of enjoying the process of mastering things which are hard to use. However, there are other types of software. We recently enjoyed reading about emulating an original Macintosh on a £0.60 chip. That’s $0.80 and of course the computer is a Raspberry Pi – but not even a Pi Zero: it’s a Pi Pico, a microcontroller. There is still some hope that the world can rediscover tiny, simple, user-centric software, built to be friendly first, and for rich functionality second. And, it almost goes without saying, hand-coded without bot assistance. Bootnote * Astounding magazine changed its name to Analog in 1960, and it’s still around. We recommend it. If you haven’t read Asimov’s original “Runaround”, that issue of Astounding is on the Internet Archive too. ®
a4f2ddf41d630dcb: SEPANG, Oct 4 — Max Verstappen claimed his first victory of the Formula One season in a chaotic Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here today, winning a race that began 1hr 40min late and only at the second attempt after torrential rain hit Sepang.
The Red Bull driver had started from pole but made a poor getaway on intermediate tyres, allowing Mercedes pair Kimi Antonelli and George Russell to sweep past him in the wet opening laps.

The race turned in Verstappen’s favour after Valtteri Bottas spun into the gravel on lap nine, bringing out the safety car as the rapidly drying circuit prompted most of the field to switch to slick tyres.
Verstappen took advantage of the restart to pass Antonelli and Russell before opening up a comfortable lead he would not relinquish.
Antonelli eventually finished second to strengthen his championship campaign, while Lewis Hamilton produced a strong recovery to claim third for Ferrari.

Hamilton had started alongside Verstappen on the front row on dry tyres but dropped down the order in the early wet conditions. The seven-time world champion worked his way back through the field as the track dried to secure a podium finish.

Russell looked set to take third before suffering late heartbreak with five laps remaining, when his Mercedes appeared to develop a power-unit problem during a late safety-car period and he was forced to retire.
Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc finished fourth, ahead of Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar in fifth, while Oscar Piastri took sixth for McLaren.

Liam Lawson was seventh for Racing Bulls, with Fernando Alonso holding off Lando Norris in the closing stages to finish eighth for Aston Martin. Norris was ninth, while Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

“72 mate, 72! Amazing job. What a fantastic weekend. Really deserved. Really good job everyone. You can be really proud of it,” Verstappen told his team over the radio after taking the chequered flag.

The race had originally been scheduled to start at 3pm but was delayed after torrential rain swept across the Sepang International Circuit shortly before lights out. A revised formation lap was initially set for 3.40pm before the race eventually got under way at 4.40pm.
Formula One returned to Sepang this weekend for the first time since 2017, when Verstappen also won at the Malaysian circuit.

2a68d654e8d44a14: OCTOBER 4 — In aviation, a lie can become an operational hazard. False information can alter a pilot's decisions, mobilise rescue services and trigger security responses with consequences for human life. Fabricating a crash or staging a hijacking therefore raises a question more serious than whether a stunt is offensive: has deception crossed the threshold into unlawful endangerment?

International law provides important answers, but precision matters. A false social-media announcement is not legally identical to a fabricated threat communicated to a flight crew. An authorised emergency exercise is different from deceiving aviation authorities. The absence of deaths does not establish innocence, just as public outrage does not establish every element of an offence. — AFP pic

International law provides important answers, but precision matters. A false social-media announcement is not legally identical to a fabricated threat communicated to a flight crew. An authorised emergency exercise is different from deceiving aviation authorities. The absence of deaths does not establish innocence, just as public outrage does not establish every element of an offence.

Article 1(1)(e) of the 1971 Montreal Convention directly addresses someone who unlawfully and intentionally communicates information they know to be false, thereby endangering an aircraft in flight. A crash is not required. Knowledge of falsity and the resulting danger to the aircraft are central. [1]

The distinction matters. A fabricated bomb warning can have legal consequences even when the aircraft lands safely. Conversely, an honestly reported concern that proves unfounded is not automatically a deliberate falsehood. Passenger distress alone cannot substitute for evidence of the danger required by this provision.

Hijacking requires a separate analysis. Under the 1970 Hague Convention, the core offence involves someone aboard an aircraft in flight unlawfully seizing or exercising control through force, threats of force or intimidation. An imaginary bomb can therefore support a real hijacking if the threat achieves the unlawful seizure of control. [2]

But a performance during which the pilot retains lawful control does not automatically establish that offence merely because passengers were deceived. Other offences may still arise. The 2010 Beijing Protocol broadens the framework, including technological means and specified threats made in circumstances indicating credibility. Treaty participation and the date of the conduct determine which framework applies. [3]

False distress communications also deserve attention. Article 47 of the International Telecommunication Union Constitution requires member states to take steps to prevent false or deceptive distress, urgency, safety or identification signals. Radio Regulations provision 15.1 prohibits false or misleading transmissions. A fabricated crash report accompanied by a false distress signal may therefore engage obligations beyond the hijacking conventions. [4]

State involvement makes the stakes greater. Article 4 of the Chicago Convention commits contracting states not to use civil aviation for purposes inconsistent with the convention's aims. Sovereignty over airspace carries responsibilities; it cannot itself legitimise manufacturing a threat for political advantage. [5]

The diversion of Ryanair Flight FR4978 to Minsk on 23 May 2021 supplies a documented institutional example. ICAO Assembly Resolution A41-1 records the Council's determination that senior Belarusian government officials knowingly participated in, or were involved in, supplying information about a false bomb threat that led to the diversion. [6]

The Assembly endorsed the determination that the government's actions deliberately endangered the aircraft and those aboard, amounting to a flagrant and serious violation of Article 4. This demonstrates the international consequences of a fabricated threat without a crash. It must, however, be distinguished from a criminal conviction of any particular individual.

State responsibility and individual criminal liability are separate questions. The International Law Commission's articles on state responsibility provide a framework for asking whether conduct is attributable to a state and breaches its international obligations. State organs, delegated governmental authority, instructions and control can be relevant. Political benefit alone does not prove attribution. [7]

If an aviation incident is fabricated to blame another country and justify military action, the United Nations Charter's prohibition on the use of force also becomes relevant. Applying its principles, a state cannot manufacture a right of self-defence from an attack it knows never occurred. A false narrative cannot supply the missing factual basis. [8]

During armed conflict, international humanitarian law distinguishes permissible ruses from perfidy. Article 37 of Additional Protocol I prohibits killing, injuring or capturing an adversary through betrayal of confidence in protection afforded by that law. Not every deception meets those requirements. Calling conduct a war crime requires proof of the relevant context and elements. [9]

The practical response should combine institutional resolve with fair process. Investigators need preserved communications, crew testimony, flight data and a reconstruction of operational decisions. Alleged state involvement requires careful examination of instructions and institutional links. Authorities must establish jurisdiction and the applicable domestic implementing law, rather than assume that every treaty permits every country to prosecute every incident.

The same evidential discipline must govern accusations that a disaster was staged. Incomplete footage, early inconsistencies or unanswered questions do not themselves establish a conspiracy. Demanding a credible explanation is legitimate. Converting uncertainty into an unsupported allegation damages the very public trust that accountability is supposed to protect.

Aviation depends on people treating emergency information as a responsibility. Deliberately exploiting that trust warrants consequences where the legal elements are proved. International law earns its authority by protecting life firmly and assessing accusations fairly. The trust that allows humanity to cross the skies must never become a prop in somebody else's performance.
*This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

913fc283182f2f6d: Decades before the modern web, the BBC Domesday Project dared to archive an entire nation using…. what else – massive LV-ROM (LaserVision Read Only Memory) LaserDiscs. To mark the impending 40th anniversary of the BBC Domesday Project's release, the UK's Centre for Computing History (CCH) hosted a celebration at its museum on September 19, bringing together several of the original team members responsible for the system. One was Mike Tibbetts, an assistant to Peter Armstrong, the BBC producer behind the project. Tibbetts revealed that the UK's domestic intelligence service, MI5, took an interest in the system, but "they didn't understand a word of what we were doing!" "And on one occasion, Peter and I had to give a presentation, or Peter gave the presentation to [former prime minister] Margaret Thatcher, and well, I'm not sure she understood what we were doing either…" What they were doing was compiling a trove of data that will prove invaluable to historians in the years to come, even if the politicians of the era looked nervously on at the amount of data being handed over to the public. The Domesday Project was intended to be a modern version of the Domesday Book, compiled after the 1066 Norman invasion of England. The original book surveyed most of England and parts of Wales and was used by the King to assess dues owed to him. 900 years later, the name was given to a project in which more than a million people participated to provide a snapshot of life in the UK. Participants (many of whom were school children) contributed content, which was linked with maps, photographs, and other data. It was all compiled onto a pair of LaserDiscs – the Community Disc and the National Disc – and accessed via a BBC Master computer and a Philips VP415 LaserVision player. Armstrong came up with the idea, and the team compiled the project between 1984 and 1986. The system was eventually released at the end of 1986, and was aimed at schools, libraries, and universities. It was, alas, not a roaring sales success – the exact price per unit is difficult to pin down, but approximately £5,000 is a fair estimate. Government subsidies lowered the cost to around £3,000, but it was still out of reach for much of its audience. As a resource, however, it has huge value, which will only increase as the years pass. Tibbetts drew parallels to the original Domesday Book, which took centuries for historians to recognize as a vital resource. "Perhaps," he mused, "40 years is simply too short a time for historians to perceive the Domesday Project as a sufficiently distant benchmark of useful research." Perhaps. However, while hundreds of years have passed since the Domesday Book was compiled, the years have not been kind to the Domesday Project, thanks to technology's inexorable march. "The original Domesday Book had one huge advantage over the Domesday Project when it comes to future-proofing and longevity," explained Tibbetts. "The vellum pages of the original Domesday have been preserved for 940 years so far, and it's likely to continue to exist well into the future. "It took very few years for the bespoke technology of the BBC Domesday Project to be overtaken by universal media technologies." However, they chose the technology at the time for good technical reasons. The BBC Micro could output a 625-line television picture. The Philips LaserVision system could be re-engineered to store alphanumeric data. There wasn't much in the way of authoring and playback systems, so, as Tibbetts explained, the team had to invent everything. "In technological terms," he said, "the world of 1984 really couldn't be more different from the instant-access, media-rich world of today." And so, inevitably, within a few short years, that technology began to show its age. "As was entirely predictable, our discs aged and became difficult to read. The expensive LV-ROM player was quickly superseded by cheaper and more widely available CD-ROM and DVD systems." And, worse, "Largely because of the lack of any great academic interest in preserving our massive resource for the future, the BBC Domesday Project was in grave danger of disappearing without a trace." Several initiatives have kicked off over the years to preserve the project, and the CCH's event was as much about celebrating those as it was about looking at the project's genesis. Tibbetts dropped some nuggets of information about the project, estimating that 60 people reported directly to him and Armstrong, with another 60 in subcontracted teams. He also discussed the frustration the team felt as doubt was cast about whether the project was even possible. "We came back from Christmas in January 1986," Tibbetts recalled, "we sat down for our first team meeting, and I was forced to point out that our little VAX minicomputer didn't have one byte of data that was ready to go onto the Domesday discs, so we did the whole thing in a few months!" As far as hardware was concerned, Andy Finney, who handled mastering the discs, remembered that the original plan for the Domesday Project was for it to be mouse-based, rather than the trackball the system used for navigation. The mouse was still a relatively novel concept, alien to many users. "I remember vividly one chap who was navigating with this mouse on the table, and he moved the mouse towards him, and by the time he got to the edge of the table, he hadn't actually reached the bottom of the screen. So he went on the edge and underneath…" Tibbetts added, "I always feel guilty about the mouse, because we got that wrong … the decision came down in favor of the trackball because that is much more easy for somebody with movement disabilities to use rather than a mouse." "But boy, did we get that wrong…" As Tibbetts noted, even with little interest from some parts of the academic community, enthusiasts have continued to put in a huge amount of effort over the years to keep the resource accessible. Simon Inns of the Domesday86 project described it as "a race against time" – not just for hardware, but to get data off discs before bit rot rendered them unreadable. The good news is that the Domesday discs have been preserved, and reside in the Internet Archive. "Anyone," said Inns, "can go to the Internet Archive and download a Domesday Disc. This is, like, groundbreaking stuff. 10 years ago, this was a laugh, right? Now you can actually do this." While there might not be many functioning examples of the hardware around anymore, the preservation efforts mean that the Domesday Project will endure. "Our hope," said Inns, "is that within the next couple of years, everyone in this room [at The Centre for Computing History] will be able to have a Domesday system and be able to experience what it was like." ®
